title: Esha Deol gets emotional as she adds late father Dharmendra's name to her credit in Pratap for the first time in 24 years
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

For Esha Deol , seeing her name on a movie poster is always special, but her soon-to-release movie Pratap has made the moment even more emotional. The star will be credited as Esha Dharmendra Deol for the first time, with her late father Dharmendra 's name appearing alongside hers. Overwhelmed by the gesture, Esha shared a heartfelt note on social media, expressing how much the moment means to her.

Adding to this, Esha Deol is over the moon as her soon-to-release movie credits her as Esha Dharmendra Deol. Esha Deol pens note about being credited as ‘Esha Dharmendra Deol’ On Monday, Esha posted on Instagram to share pictures of her movie posters displayed on billboards across the city. Alongside the pictures, she penned a note that read, "My first movie as Esha Dharmendra Deol. To see Papa’s name next to mine on a movie poster for the first time feels deeply emotional, personal & overwhelming. With Papa’s blessings, here I am. 🪽🥹♥️ 24 years in the movie industry & counting."
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by ESHA DHARMENDRA DEOL (@imeshadeol)

Notably, She added, "Even after all these years, seeing myself on billboards outside cinema halls still fills me with the same joy I felt when I started. All I can say is Gratitude, gratitude, gratitude to all my followers and well-wishers. Thank you for showing up for me, for all the love you’ve given me over the years, and for the love you continue to give me and my family."

As per the latest buzz, Veteran star Dharmendra passed away on November 24, 2025, aged 89, leaving behind a legacy spanning more than six decades and over 300 films. Several Bollywood actors, including Salman Khan, Shah Rukh Khan and Amitabh Bachchan, paid tribute to the veteran star following his demise.

In further updates, In January this year, Sunny Deol also paid a special tribute to his father through the opening credits of Border 2. Instead of his usual screen credit, he was introduced as 'Sunny Deol (Dharmendra ji ka beta)' (Dharmendra's son). The gesture moved audiences, as Sunny chose to acknowledge his identity as Dharmendra's son on the big screen. He also became emotional while talking about the tribute, saying that he would always remain his father's son.

On top of that, Directed by Sachin Saraf and backed by Pradeep Rangwani, Pratap is an action thriller starring Amit Sadh, Esha Deol, Tigmanshu Dhulia, Seema Biswas, Milind Gunaji and Dushyant Wagh in key roles.

The story follows Pratap Ranade, a decorated encounter specialist whose world turns upside down after a video of him is leaked. Framed for murder by the very system he once served, he goes on the run to evade his former police colleagues and expose a deep-rooted state conspiracy linked to his past record. The movie is scheduled to rollout in theatres on November 20.

title: Oldest living James Bond actor George Lazenby congratulates Robert Pattinson on becoming 007, shares advice
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

George Lazenby has welcomed Robert Pattinson to the James Bond franchise after Amazon MGM Studios officially revealed his casting as the next 007. The 87-year-old star, the oldest living star to have played the iconic spy, shared a video message for Pattinson on social media, offering him some advice as he prepares to take over the role from Daniel Craig.

Adding to this, George Lazenby shared a video on Instagram and welcomed Robert Pattinson to James Bond club. George Lazenby welcomes Robert Pattinson to James Bond club George posted on Instagram hours after the announcement to congratulate the Batman star. In the video, he shared, “Robert, welcome to the most exclusive club in the world. But remember to enjoy yourself. Let’s see if you’ll have [your] ‘this never happened to the other fella’ moment.”
Meanwhile, He signed off with, “All the best mate, George.”
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by George Lazenby (@georgelazenbyofficial)

As per the latest buzz, George Lazenby played James Bond in just one movie, On Her Majesty’s Secret Service, rolled out in 1969. He stepped into the role after Sean Connery, who had played the British spy in the first five official Bond films. George's portrayal was followed by Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan and Daniel Craig.

In further updates, Amazon MGM Studios verified Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond on Monday, November 16. The announcement came through the official 007 social media accounts, which shared a video and a photograph of the star in a black tuxedo holding a gun. The reveal was accompanied by the message, “Identity verified.”

On top of that, Pattinson, 40, succeeds Daniel Craig, whose final appearance as the British spy was in the 2021 movie No Time to Die. The casting makes Pattinson the seventh star to play Bond in the official movie franchise.

Reacting to the announcement, Pattinson shared in a note through Variety, “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime. I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”

title: Ananya Panday addresses debate on nepotism; says, “I am very proud to be my father’s daughter”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

During the conversation, Ananya also spoke about the stereotypes associated with Generation Z. Responding to perceptions that young people are lazy, entitled or unwilling to put in long working hours, the star defended her generation and shared that its approach towards success was different from that of previous generations.

Adding to this, “I think Gen Z is badnaam for no reason honestly!” she shared. Explaining her perspective, she added, “Just the definition of success is different. Maybe for the old generation, while growing up, there was only one kind of success. You had to follow a certain path to get that. Gen Z is a little different. I thrive on chaos, love working for as many hours as possible. But maybe someone else in my generation is equally successful and doesn’t work as hard. That’s their way of doing it," she added.

Meanwhile, The discussion also touched upon the nepotism debate, which has remained a part of conversations around Ananya ever since her entry into Bollywood. Addressing the subject, the star shared she saw no reason to distance herself from her family background or her father's identity. She also expressed her admiration for Chunky Panday and shared she did not want her association with him to carry any negative connotations.

title: Ramayana, Dhurandhar 2 propel Indian box office past ₹15000 crore in 2026, giving Indian cinema's highest-grossing year ever
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Indian cinema has come a long way since the barren days of the COVID-19 pandemic and lockdowns. 2020 and 2021 were the two worst years in Indian cinema history in terms of box-office collections. It took the collective might of all language industries to revive theatrical business. And now, in 2026, the ticket-window juggernaut has rolled past ₹ 15,000 crore rupees for the first time. This marks a complete turnaround for an industry that was written off just five years ago.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor in Ramayana (L) and Ranveer Singh in Dhurandhar The Revenge (R). 2026: Indian cinema’s highest-grossing year Box-office tracking data from Sacnilk reveals that Indian films have had their best year at the ticket-window in a long time in 2026. As of November 15, six weeks before the year ends, Indian films have collected ₹ 11,789 crore rupees net at the domestic ticket-window and ₹ 15,637 crore rupees gross worldwide. This is the first time Indian films have crossed this threshold, having stopped marginally short of the mark in 2025. In both 2023 and 2024, the estimated worldwide collection of Indian films was under ₹ 13,000 crore rupees.

Meanwhile, So far, 1263 films have rolled out in India this year - 1141 Indian and 122 foreign. The Indian films contributed to ₹ 15,637 crore rupees gross worldwide. This record collection comes on the back of the stupendous runs of Dhurandhar: The Revenge and Ramayana , which have collectively collected over ₹ 3,000 crore rupees. These two films alone account for over 20% of the total gross. The two films, along with other successes like Border 2, Mirzapur, and Drishyam 3, kept Bollywood ’s flag flying high in 2026.

Notably, Tamil cinema also gave its highest-grosser with Rajinikanth’s Jailer 2, an ₹ 835-crore rupees smash hit, along with three other ₹ 200-crore rupees hits, all starring Suriya, the most consistent star of the year. Malayalam cinema also saw a record-breaking run from Bethlehem Kudumba Unit, a ₹ 330-crore rupees hit. But Telugu and Kannada films did not fare as well. The biggest releases in both languages - Peddi and Toxic, respectively - were massive box-office bombs.

As per the latest buzz, One of the highlights of this year’s Indian ticket-window success was the success of small- and mid-budget films. Hanuman Ansh, a devotional movie made on a budget of just ₹ 2 crore rupees, was the year’s biggest success story, minting over ₹ 440 crore rupees. It is the most profitable Indian movie ever. Mirzapur: The Movie was also a surprise hit. With no stars, it defied conventional wisdom and brought a web series' success to the big screen, minting ₹ 325 crore rupees. Bethlehem Kudumba Unit, the biggest Malayalam hit of the year, was also made on a modest budget of just ₹ 25 crore rupees. It grossed 13 times as much at the ticket-window.

In further updates, Indian films’ total contribution at the domestic ticket-window was ₹ 12,247 crore rupees gross this year. A substantial number - over ₹ 1500 crore rupees - came from foreign releases. The wrecker-in-chief here was Spider-Man : Brand New Day. The Marvel-Sony joint production collected ₹ 503 crore rupees net ( ₹ 594 crore rupees gross) in India, a figure that only a handful of Indian films have surpassed. Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey also scored big, minting over ₹ 200 crore rupees. But the real surprise was how niche horror did in India. Obsession collected almost ₹ 100 crore rupees gross, leading this list.

On top of that, In the six weeks that remain of 2026, there are a few big releases lined up, notably Shah Rukh Khan ’s King, the star’s first rollout in over three years. The action entertainer is being seen as the tentpole that could help Indian cinema end the year on a high. The last time SRK and director Sidharth Anand collaborated, it resulted in Pathaan, a ₹ 1050-crore rupees smash hit. The two would hope for an encore.

title: John Abraham makes a STRONG appeal to tourists visiting Meghalaya: “For heaven’s sake, DON’T dirty the place!”; reveals that the North-Eastern state will soon have India’s BIGGEST football stadium
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

While interacting with the media, John Abraham spoke passionately about his association with Meghalaya. He shared, “The government of Meghalaya has been kind enough to give us 20 acres of land. On that land, we are building a state-of-the-art academy, primarily for football and then for other sports.”
Adding to this, On a serious note, he confessed, “It’s my desire to design a world-class academy where we can groom young footballers so that they can play at an international level.”

Meanwhile, John Abraham continued, “I am very excited to present this very beautiful state to you that is arguably the most searched state today in India. It’s got beautiful locations. Connectivity is at its best now. Meghalaya itna duur nahin hai. Aap jaa sakte ho wahaan pe . I consider it my home. We house our football there and soon, we are also going to have our academy.”

Notably, He also revealed, “Shillong is soon going to have India’s biggest football stadium. It has a capacity of 40,000 spectators. It’s 70-80% ready. It’s of international standards, at par with prominent stadiums across the world. I have seen our academy spot as well. It’s just 500 metres away from the stadium. That way, we are lucky! So, please come and watch football games there in the future (smiles).”

As per the latest buzz, John then spoke about the cleanliness of Meghalaya and made a candid observation. He shared, “Meghalaya is very clean. I am sorry to say, but we must learn a sense of hygiene and we must learn to be clean as people. If you walk around Meghalaya anywhere, you’ll see that it’s so clean.”

In further updates, When a journalist asked whether the state offers sufficient food options for vegetarians and vegans, John clarified, “I have a lot of vegans and vegetarians in my team. You also get the best vegan and vegetarian food in Meghalaya. So, food is not a problem in that state at all.”

On top of that, Highlighting the state's vibrant music scene, he further shared, “In Meghalaya, there are as many as 3,000 to 4,000 live bands playing. That’s the level of music and culture the state has.”

Later, while addressing the gathering from the dais, John Abraham once again stressed the importance of keeping Meghalaya clean. Making a strong appeal to tourists, he shared, “For heaven’s sake, don’t dirty the place! Meghalaya is a very clean state. We are known for our hygiene. So, please make sure we don’t dirty that state. Keep it clean; keep it pristine.”

title: Avengers: Doomsday creates HISTORY; emerges as the FIRST film to open midnight show bookings ONE MONTH before release; shows already filling FAST
body: Here's the latest update from the Hollywood/Marvel world:

What makes this development remarkable and even historic is that cinemas have begun selling tickets for post-midnight shows right from the start. Usually, theatres first open bookings for shows during normal hours. Midnight shows are added on the day of rollout, depending on demand. In the case of Oppenheimer (2023), midnight screenings were added much later, more than 10 days after advance bookings had commenced and 2-3 days before rollout. However, Avengers: Doomsday has taken things to another level. In a rare development, bookings have opened more than a month in advance for shows beginning as early as 12:00 am. What's more, several of these screenings are already filling up rapidly.

Adding to this, Most of these early screenings are for the English version in Infinity Vision 3D. In Mumbai, PVR Lower Parel has scheduled shows at 12:05 am and 3:05 am. Similarly, Miraj Wadala will screen the movie at 12:05 am and 3:05 am. PVR Sangam Andheri has shows at 12:05 am and 3:25 am, while INOX Raghuleela Kandivali has scheduled screenings at the same timings. At Cinepolis Viviana Mall, Thane, moviegoers can catch the movie at 12:01 am. Meanwhile, PVR Infiniti Malad has scheduled a show at 3:15 am. In Delhi-NCR, Gurugram's Cinepolis Airia Mall and Cinepolis Grand View High Street have scheduled shows at 12:05 am and 12:15 am, respectively.

Meanwhile, In Ahmedabad, Cinepolis Nexus has opened bookings for an 11:59 am show. This means that the screening will technically take place on December 16, a day before the movie's official rollout. Meanwhile, Cinepolis Vastral is the only cinema in India to have opened bookings for a 12:10 am show in the regular 2D format instead of Infinity Vision 3D.

Notably, As for Surat, PVR Rahul Raj is the only theatre in India to have opened bookings for a 2:15 am show in Infinity Vision 3D, that too in Hindi. Other post-midnight screenings include Kolkata's Cinepolis Lake Mall (12:00 am and 12:10 am) and Cinepolis Acropolis Mall (12:25 am), as well as Vadodara's INOX Race Course Circle (12:05 am and 3:25 am).

As per the latest buzz, Of course, moviegoers can also watch the movie during normal hours. However, this is just the beginning. Looking at the response, there's little doubt that more cinemas will soon add screenings between 12:00 am and 6:00 am to accommodate the growing demand.

In further updates, The only downside is the IMAX situation. Dune: Part Three , which releases in the same week (Friday, December 18), has secured exclusive IMAX screenings in major markets, leaving Avengers: Doomsday without an IMAX rollout. Nevertheless, the early rush for midnight shows indicates that the superhero extravaganza could emerge as one of the biggest openers ever in India.

On top of that, Apart from Dune: Part Three , Jumanji: Open World and the much-awaited Shah Rukh Khan-starrer King are also arriving in the second half of December. With four massive films battling for audiences, expect 2026 to end with a bang.

title: Ramayana worldwide box office collection day 12: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash's film storms past ₹1400 crore; outpaces Dhurandhar 2, Baahubali 2
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana may have lost the festive momentum at the ticket-window, but the movie refuses to slow down even on weekdays. On its third Monday, the movie saw its first big drop in collections as the festive cheer and the weekend ended. Yet, the Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer had enough legs to mint ₹ 50 crore rupees worldwide, a solid number for any Monday, let alone the third. This has kept the mythological epic as the best-paced Indian movie in the first two weeks of rollout.

Adding to this, Yash plays Ravana in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana. Ramayana worldwide ticket-window update The Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer had seven consecutive days where it grossed over ₹ 100 crore rupees worldwide. That run came to an end last Thursday, before Saturday and Sunday propped Ramayana up again. On Monday, the penny finally dropped. The movie collected ₹ 32 crore rupees net in India on its 12th day, a 57% drop from the Sunday haul of ₹ 75 crore rupees. But by no means was the day disappointing for the movie. A drop of less than 60% for such a big movie is a sign that audience interest remains. After 12 days, Ramayana’s domestic haul now stands at ₹ 792 crore rupees net ( ₹ 947 crore rupees gross).

Meanwhile, Overseas, Ramayana turned over a new leaf after a subpar start. As the movie followed its staggered rollout in additional international markets, the numbers began to grow. Thanks to a solid showing in the US and in niche markets like Thailand, Vietnam, and Nepal, Ramayana has now collected over $51 million overseas. This takes the movie’s worldwide gross to ₹ 1437 crore rupees after 12 days. The movie is now the fifth-highest-grossing in Indian cinema history.

Notably, Ramayana reached ₹ 1400 crore rupees in just 12 days, the fastest for an Indian movie ever. At the end of 12 days, Ranveer Singh’s Dhurandhar The Revenge had collected ₹ 1394 crore rupees worldwide, while Allu Arjun’s Pushpa 2: The Rule was further behind with collections of ₹ 1335 crore rupees. SS Rajamouli’s Baahubali 2 was way back at around ₹ 1100 crore rupees. With Ramayana outpacing all these blockbusters, there is hope that the movie can surpass their lifetime hauls and breach the elusive ₹ 2000-crore rupees mark.

As per the latest buzz, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is the first of a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravie Dubey as Lakshman. The first part is running in theatres, while the second part is set for a Diwali 2028 rollout.

title: All Indian Cine Workers Association thanks Salman Khan and Sonu Sood for helping Sharad Kapoor, urges film industry to support struggling artists
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

After Josh star Sharad Kapoor 's emotional plea for work went widely shared on social media, actors Sonu Sood and Salman Khan stepped in to help him. The All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) has now expressed its gratitude to Sonu and Salman for standing by Sharad during a difficult phase in his life. In a statement, the association thanked Salman for providing financial assistance and Sonu for as per reports offering him work opportunities and arranging medical support.

Adding to this, AICWA thanks Salman Khan and Sharad Kapoor for supporting Sharad Kapoor in difficult time. AICWA praises Sonu Sood and Salman Khan On Monday, AICWA shared a statement on Instagram, expressing gratitude to Salman and Sonu. The movie body also appealed to successful members of the industry to come forward and help artists in need. The statement read, "The All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) warmly thanks Salman Khan for coming forward to support star Sharad Kapoor with financial help in this difficult time. Such a gesture gives hope not only to Sharad Kapoor ji, but to every artist who fears being forgotten in his hard days."
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by All Indian Cine Workers Association (@aicwaofficial)

Notably, The association added, "AICWA also extends its heartfelt gratitude to Sonu Sood for reaching out to Sharad Kapoor ji. Sonu Sood ji has as per reports met him to discuss a project that could bring him back to work, and has also arranged medical support for him. Work, with dignity, is exactly what Sharad Kapoor ji asked for."

As per the latest buzz, AICWA also noted that Sharad had worked in films alongside stars such as Shah Rukh Khan and Hrithik Roshan and was once in demand. It shared he now needed the industry's support and lauded Salman and Sonu for standing by him during a difficult time. The association thanked them on behalf of the movie fraternity and urged successful names in Indian cinema to follow their example and help artists and industry workers in need. It also pointed out that many others like Sharad were silently battling difficult circumstances.

In further updates, The statement further read, "Bad times have come to many in Bollywood before, and they will come again. Not everyone faces them, only a few, and they never announce their arrival. Today it has come to Sharad Kapoor ji. Those of us who are doing well today must think of these few, because they are a part of our Indian cinema family. Humanity, and it is our duty. 'Sharad Kapoor ji, you are not alone. The entire industry is with you.' Everyone in Indian cinema is a part of one family. We must stand with each other, in good times and in bad. If we do not stand by our own, who will?"
On top of that, According to a report in India Today, Sharad verified that, apart from Sonu Sood and Salman Khan, Amitabh Bachchan had also reached out to him following his social media post.

Star Sharad Kapoor of late found himself at the centre of social media attention after an emotional video showing him parting ways with his four pet dogs went widely shared. Sharad temporarily moved his dogs, Josh, Rebel, Star and Panther, to a welfare centre run by the Youth Organization in Defence of Animals (YODA) in Mumbai. title: Over 230 films to be screened at IFFI 2026 in Goa; Dhurandhar to open, Spain named Country of Honour
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The 57th edition of the International Movie Festival of India ( IFFI ) will be held in Goa from November 20 to 28, with over 230 movies from the host country as well as across the world set to be screened under the theme 'Stories Without Borders'.

Adding to this, Ranveer Singh in a still from Dhurandhar. Announcing this on Monday, chief minister Pramod Sawant shared Spain has been designated the Country of Honour, while Russia will be the Partner Country for the nine-day festival, whose opening films will be Dhurandhar and Becoming.

Meanwhile, Addressing a press conference in Goa, Sawant noted the festival would bring together filmmakers, artistes, industry professionals and cinema enthusiasts from across the globe, reaffirming Goa's position as an important destination for international cinematic and cultural exchange.

Notably, More than 230 films, including over 150 international movies from 86 countries, will be screened at the annual festival across six venues comprising 13 screens, with a combined seating capacity of over 4,000 delegates, he informed.

As per the latest buzz, The screening venues are INOX Panjim, Maquinez Palace, INOX Porvorim, Z Square Samrat-Ashok, Magic Moviez in Ponda and Ravindra Bhavan in Margao. All venues will have accessibility facilities for persons with disabilities.

In further updates, The festival will feature the participation of 52 women moviemakers and 62 debut filmmakers. The sixth edition of Creative Minds of Tomorrow (CMOT) will bring together 100 selected participants representing 13 filmmaking crafts.
On top of that, The opening and closing ceremonies will be held at the Dr Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Indoor Stadium near Panaji on November 20 and 28, respectively.

The festival will also host 14 masterclasses, workshops, panel discussions, retrospectives and interactive sessions at the Kala Academy from November 21 to 27, featuring personalities from the movie industry, according to the CM.

title: E. Niwas returns to feature films with Kurla Boyz, a supernatural comedy backed by Abundantia Entertainment
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The story follows a street-smart young man from Kurla who falls in love with a girl from a family believed to be under a generations-old curse. Hoping to break it, he brings together his group of friends for an adventure involving love, friendship and supernatural encounters. The movie aims to capture the everyday life, language and culture of the Mumbai neighbourhood through a comedy-driven narrative.

Adding to this, Speaking about the project, director E. Niwas shared, “What draws me to Kurla Boyz is the unique world the movie is set in. Kurla has a spirit and a rhythm that hasn’t really been explored on screen, and I wanted to capture that. At its core, this is a story about friendship, the kind where your friends will chase a ghost for you, and about the chaotic fun that comes with it. I am thrilled to be working with Abundantia Entertainment and One Entertainment Films to take this fun ride to the world.”
Meanwhile, A post shared by Abundantia Entertainment (@abundantiaent)
Notably, Vikram Malhotra, Founder and CEO of Abundantia Entertainment, shared the movie was an attempt to connect with younger audiences through a story rooted in a distinct Mumbai setting.

As per the latest buzz, “At Abundantia, we want to connect with young audiences through stories that speak in their voices, reach them impactfully and connect on their home turf. Kurla Boyz does exactly that. The setting is incredible. Kurla has a flavour like no other, and the movie shows the city’s underbelly the way its residents see it: full of life, colour and heart. With E. Niwas at the helm and One Entertainment co-producing, we are excited to bring this unique story to audiences,” he shared.

In further updates, Kamal Kishor Mishra, Founder of One Entertainment Films, also shared his thoughts on the collaboration. “I am delighted to partner with Abundantia Entertainment and E. Niwas on Kurla Boyz. This is going to be a movie that the youth audience will take up in big numbers, owing to its relatable themes as well as for its dialled-up entertainment,” he shared.
On top of that, The movie’s script is ready, and casting is currently underway. The makers are expected to announce further details about the cast and production in the coming months.

title: Ramayana box office collection day 12: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash’s epic inches towards ₹800 crore milestone despite 57% drop on second Monday
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Ramayana continues its impressive run at the ticket-window, drawing audiences to theatres even as it enters its second week. The mythological epic, starring Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana, has maintained a strong hold across several markets, with its Hindi version leading collections and the dubbed versions contributing to its pan-India performance. Despite witnessing a drop in daily earnings, the movie has continued to add substantial numbers to its overall collection and is now closing in on several major ticket-window milestones.

Adding to this, Ramayana ticket-window earnings: Ranbir Kapoor’s movie earns ₹32 crore rupees on Day 12, trails Dhurandhar 2 in India net collections. Ramayana ticket-window earnings According to trade tracker Sacnilk, on day 12, Ramayana collected ₹ 32 crore rupees net in India across 22,365 shows. The Hindi version accounted for the largest share, earning ₹ 23.75 crore rupees from 17,742 shows. The Malayalam version followed with ₹ 2.85 crore rupees from 1,061 shows, while the Kannada version collected ₹ 2 crore rupees from 892 shows. The Tamil version added ₹ 1.90 crore rupees from 1,158 shows, and the Telugu version contributed ₹ 1.50 crore rupees from 1,512 shows.

Meanwhile, The movie recorded a 57.3% drop compared to its day 11 collection. However, its overall numbers remain strong. With the latest earnings, Ramayana's India net total stands at ₹ 792.60 crore rupees. With its second-week run underway, Ramayana will be looking to maintain its momentum in the days ahead.

Notably, Ramayana: Part 1, rolled out in a few regions as Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, is directed by Nitesh Tiwari, who co-wrote the screenplay with Shridhar Raghavan. It is produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash. The movie also stars Ravie Dubey , Addinath Kothare, Lara Dutta, Vivek Oberoi, Rakul Preet Singh, Indira Krishnan, Arun Govil, among others. It is based on multiple iterations of the epic, including the Valmiki Ramayana. The second of the movie, which will also star Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman, will arrive in cinemas in 2028.

As per the latest buzz, The movie's ticket-window success is not its only recent achievement. Ramayana: Part 1 will also be the first movie screened in the BRICS segment at the 57th edition of the International Movie Festival of India (IFFI), which is scheduled to begin in Goa on November 20. According to the Press Information Bureau (PIB), the segment will feature films from all 11 BRICS member countries, as well as partner nations. The initiative aims to bring films from around the world to Indian audiences and showcase a range of cinematic styles and stories.

title: Amitabh Bachchan, Abhishek Bachchan receive death threats from gangster Goldy Dhillon; claims 200 associates are active in Mumbai
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

In his post, Dhillon claimed that the arrests of Vikas Thakur and Deepak Singh would not affect the alleged plan to target Amitabh Bachchan in Mumbai. He also claimed that around 200 of his associates were active in the city. The post named both Amitabh and Abhishek, warning that their security arrangements would not prevent an attack.

Adding to this, “No matter how many bulletproof cabins they build, they will be shot,” the post shared. Dhillon also referred to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots and threatened people who, according to him, had made statements against the Sikh community. The authenticity of the post and the claims made in it have not been independently verified.

Meanwhile, The threat follows the arrest of Vikas Thakur, alias Vicky, from Jalandhar, and Deepak Singh, alias Deep, from Tarn Taran in Punjab. The Delhi Police Special Cell arrested the two men on Saturday. Investigators suspect that they were involved in separate but potentially connected plans, including an alleged conspiracy to open fire outside Amitabh Bachchan’s Mumbai residence, Jalsa.

Notably, According to the information shared about the investigation, Thakur was allegedly assigned to shoot a Delhi-based businessman as part of an extortion attempt. He had as per reports travelled from Mumbai for the operation, while Singh was expected to join him later.

As per the latest buzz, The latest threat comes amid multiple security alerts involving Jalsa. The Mumbai residence was as per reports named in three bomb threat emails over the past month. On November 1, Amitabh greeted followers during his customary Sunday appearance from behind a bulletproof glass enclosure, instead of his usual open pedestal.

It tells the story of a lovable gangster who fools his father into believing that he is a doctor. However, when his father discovers the truth and is left heartbroken, Munna decides to enrol in a medical college and become a doctor for real, leading to hilarious situations, madness and chaos.

title: Ananya Panday on the nepotism debate: I am proud to be my father's daughter; thank God every day I get to live my dream
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Lazy, entitled and unwilling to put in the hours? Ananya Panday isn’t buying the stereotypes surrounding Gen Z. The 28-year-old star, speaking at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in New Delhi on Saturday, had a spirited defence of her generation.

Adding to this, Ananya Panday “I think Gen Z is badnaam for no reason honestly!” she shared, adding that the younger generation simply defines success differently. “Just the definition of success is different. Maybe for the old generation, while growing up, there was only one kind of success. You had to follow a certain path to get that. Gen Z is a little different. I thrive on chaos, love working for as many hours as possible. But maybe someone else in my generation is equally successful and doesn’t work as hard. That’s their way of doing it," she added.

Meanwhile, The conversation inevitably turned to nepotism, a debate that has followed Ananya since her Bollywood debut in Student of the Year 2 (2019). But the star isn’t shying away from her privilege or her father, star Chunky Panday’s legacy.

Notably, “I think there’s no point in not acknowledging it. I am very proud to be my father’s daughter. I don’t ever not want to be associated with Chunky Panday, so I don’t want to have any negative connotation with that association,” she shared, adding, “Contrary to whatever people may believe about me, I wake up every day and thank God I get to live my dream. I am lucky, privileged.”

As per the latest buzz, As for the current atmosphere of fear in the movie industry post the threats issued to Tiger Shroff, Ananya shared, “It’s very scary. This will make people less lax about safety measures for everyone involved; I don’t think it’s just about actors’ safety, but crowds’ safety too.”

title: Exclusive| Where did the OG Bollywood rom-coms go, asks Taapsee Pannu
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

As a ’90s kid, star Taapsee Pannu misses the rom-coms that Bollywood was known for. Now, she feels Bollywood’s romances could do with less attention to camera angles and more to the person across the frame.

Adding to this, Taapsee Pannu “I don’t want to see the same trope — mummy-papa nahi maan rahe, difference in religion and caste — conflicts of the ’90s. I want to see rom-coms representing today’s issues; the process of falling in love has changed thanks to technology,” she says.

Meanwhile, While she is associated with the more serious parts, the star says she is open to a love story next. She says, “Ofcourse I want to play someone dramatic and filmy. We dont have to try too hard, having grown up in this country and the 90s films all of us have that filmy-ness in us. People haven't seen e doing that genre much and it will be new for the audience too.”

Notably, For Taapsee , the problem also lies in how actors approach romance: “Back in the day when people did romantic movies, it felt like these two people can only see each other in their lives. Today, with the increasing demand for vanity, actors are always second-guessing how they are looking on camera, wondering what the best angles are.”

As per the latest buzz, Nor, she feels, does every love story need a dark twist or social message. She would welcome another movie like Manmarziyaan (2018), which viewers still discuss with her. “I'm not saying it was a big box-office success but it's one movie that achieved cult status of sorts. Even today people tell me they are happy I did that movie and that they rewatch it. It was made ahead of time like many of Anurag's (Kashyap) films. It was a pure love story with any darkness or social message.”

In further updates, Sharing her thoughts on the need of the hour she says, “One wants to show heroism over being submissive and looking like you can do anything for the girl, or it goes to a toxic extreme. The whole in-between part where you show love for the other person is missing."

On top of that, Her own relationship with husband, former badminton player Mathias Boe, remains decidedly old school. “It’s been 13 years that I’ve been with my partner. Even back then I wanted someone who would make an effort, who would go out of the way to do things for me. There was nothing called benching or situationship that featured in my scheme of things. Thankfully, he felt the same, and we were on the same page,” she shares.

title: Imtiaz Ali defends star kids, says ‘they have a terrible disadvantage: a very high parameter of success’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Should Jab We Met (2007) get a sequel? Absolutely, says filmmaker Imtiaz Ali . But there’s a catch: he doesn’t want to direct it! Speaking with Sonal Kalra, HT’s Chief Managing Editor for Entertainment and Lifestyle at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in New Delhi on Saturday, the 55-year-old shared, “I think there should be a Jab We Met 2, but someone else should make it. Why shouldn’t I get the chance to watch and enjoy a Jab We Met?”

Adding to this, Imtiaz Ali But would Kareena Kapoor Khan’s much-loved Geet be any different in today’s social media-driven world? “It might have been exactly the same. It is very difficult to capture the adventure of a modern relationship in a cinematic manner… if she has to be a social media influencer, she will be sitting on a couch and going through her phone, which won’t look interesting. We want to see actors looking and doing interesting stuff. There is that paradox,” he shared.

Meanwhile, The filmmaker, who has his next O Saathi Re lined up for rollout on Netflix, also weighed in on the nepotism debate, defending actors born into movie families. “Being a second-generation movie person, they have a terrible disadvantage: they have a very high parameter of success,” he shared, citing Ananya Panday’s family background. He added, “When she has to work and do a shot well, there is nothing that her father or anybody in her family has done, which will help her at that point. People outside the movie industry don’t understand how hard an star works.”

title: The Vvaan 2 announced on Chhath Puja, Ektaa Kapoor to take Sidharth Malhotra and Tamannaah Bhatia's folklore fantasy forward with a new universe
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The story of The Vvaan is not over yet. Ektaa Kapoor has revealed its sequel, The Vvaan 2, on the occasion of Chhath Puja. Following the first movie's theatrical run, the makers are now ready to return to its mysterious world and take the story further. Directed by Deepak Kumar Mishra, the first instalment featured Sidharth Malhotra and Tamannaah Bhatia.

Adding to this, Filmmaker and producer Ektaa R Kapoor has revealed a sequel to her 2026 folklore fantasy movie, The Vvaan, titled The Vvaan 2. The world of Vvaan expands Balaji Motion Pictures and The Widely shared Fever (TVF), who came together for the first movie, are reuniting for the sequel. However, the plan goes beyond continuing the original story. The makers are now looking to expand The Vvaan into a larger universe, with more characters and stories drawn from Indian folklore and mythology.

Meanwhile, Chhath Puja seemed like a fitting occasion for the announcement, given the festival's strong connection with Bihar and its place in the first movie. The makers also rolled out a teaser showing a little girl following a butterfly into a forest. Announcing the next chapter, the makers wrote, "THE VVAAN ki kahaani abhi baaki hai…..", suggesting that the story of this mysterious forest is far from over.

Notably, Despite receiving mixed reviews from critics, the first movie managed to deliver steady box-office performance. It collected around ₹ 92.48 crore rupees worldwide, making it one of Sidharth's highest-grossing films in the post-pandemic period.

As per the latest buzz, The star of late opened up about how the movie found an audience despite initial doubts about its box-office prospects, and why he believes stories rooted in Indian culture are connecting with moviegoers. On Koffee With Karan 9, Karan brought up The Vvaan: Force of the Forrest and pointed out that there had been considerable chatter about the movie underperforming at the ticket-window.

In further updates, Sidharth acknowledged the scepticism around the fantasy adventure, which rolled out in September 2026. "I think they are doing their job and we are doing our job," Sidharth shared. “There is an India, and there is a Bharat. I think Bharat is what is coming out to watch our films. They want to watch something rooted, something to them and rooted in culture. The Vvaan came perfectly fitting that bracket whether it is the writing, performance, whether it was sequences.”

On top of that, The Vvaan: Force of the Forrest draws from the folklore surrounding the Van Devi Temple near Bihta in Bihar. Sidharth plays Rishi, a Mumbai-based man who travels to the village of Devanchal with his wife Mamta (Tamannaah Bhatia) for a land-related matter. This begins as a routine visit, but it turns into something far more unsettling when he learns about the village's age-old beliefs, particularly the warning against entering the forest after dark. The movie is currently streaming on Prime Video.

title: Harshvardhan Rane gets ₹3.5 crore luxury car from Sanam Teri Kasam producer, asks him to approve film's sequel
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Star Harshvardhan Rane of late posted on Instagram to share that Sanam Teri Kasam producer Deepak Mukut had kept his promise and gifted him a luxury car worth over ₹ 3.5 crore rupees. The star shared a picture of Mukut handing him the keys to a new Land Rover Defender Octa, which is as per reports priced at over ₹ 3.5 crore rupees in India.

Adding to this, Sanam Teri Kasam producer gifts luxury car to Harshvardhan Rane. Harshvardhan Rane receives luxury car from Sanam Teri Kasam producer Deepak Mukut shared a picture of himself gifting Harshvardhan the new vehicle and wrote, “Harsh, thank you for standing by our movie last year with the re-rollout of #sanamterikasam. Just as you stood by the movie last year, today I stand by my word. A promise is a promise, and this is a small gesture of my appreciation.”

Meanwhile, Harshvardhan reshared the post on Instagram and urged the producer to make Sanam Teri Kasam 2. Thanking Mukut for keeping his word, the star wrote, “Deepak Sir I’ve been part of many promises, but you stand apart. You’re truly a man of your word. Sir, just as I stood outside your office (Soham Rockstar Entertainment) last year, alongside followers requesting the re-rollout of Sanam Teri Kasam, I’ll be back at your doorstep with them on my birthday next month. This time, with one request: your approval for Sanam Teri Kasam 2. Script and Director of your choice! Will you grant me and the followers this birthday wish, sir? ❤️.”
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Harshvardhan Rane (@harshvardhanrane)

As per the latest buzz, Sanam Teri Kasam, directed by Radhika Rao and Vinay Sapru, was originally rolled out in theatres on February 5, 2016. The movie starred Harshvardhan Rane and Pakistani star Mawra Hocane in the lead roles, with Harshvardhan playing Inder and Mawra portraying Saru.

In further updates, The movie failed to make an impact at the ticket-window during its original theatrical run, collecting around ₹ 8 crore rupees in India and declared a ticket-window flop. However, it gradually developed a loyal fan after its rollout on digital platforms.

On top of that, Nine years after its original rollout, the movie returned to theatres on February 7, 2025. Its re-rollout received an unexpectedly strong response, with the movie collecting around ₹ 4.25 crore rupees on its opening day in India. It went on to earn over ₹ 42 crore rupees in India net collection, while its worldwide gross collection stood at approximately ₹ 54 crore rupees. The movie's box-office success made it one of the biggest success stories among Indian movie re-releases.

title: HT Exclusive: Sunny Deol's Suryaa postponed amid controversy over doctors' portrayal and CBFC delay, makers refuse to compromise on film's vision
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Sunny Deol 's soon-to-release movie Suryaa : Ant Se Aarambh Tak has been postponed and will no longer hit theatres on November 20 as scheduled. The makers have decided to hold back the rollout until the movie receives certification from the Central Board of Movie Certification ( CBFC ). The move comes amid objections from members of the medical fraternity over the movie's portrayal of doctors. Meanwhile, the Delhi High Court has declined to hear another PIL seeking a stay on the movie's rollout, noting that a similar plea is already being heard by a different bench.

Adding to this, Sunny Deol's Suryaa delays theatrical rollout amid doctors' objections; new date to be revealed after CBFC clearance. Sunny Deol's Suryaa postponed Confirming the delay to Hindustan Times, the makers shared they wanted Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak to rollout in the form they had originally envisioned. They also appealed to the media and members of the medical fraternity to watch the entire movie before judging it on the basis of its teaser or promotional clips.

Meanwhile, In an official statement, the team shared the rollout had been pushed as the movie was yet to complete the certification process. A fresh date will be revealed once it receives the required clearance. The makers also responded to the criticism over certain scenes in the promotional material. They pointed out that opinions about the movie's story and intent were being formed even though the complete movie had not been screened for those raising concerns, except for the certification authorities. They maintained that a few seconds of footage cannot give viewers a fair understanding of the characters, the larger narrative or what the movie ultimately wants to convey.

Notably, Presented by Kamal Mukut, Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak is the Hindi remake of the Malayalam movie Joseph, which was well received by critics and audiences. The Hindi version has been adapted for a new audience while keeping the emotional depth and investigative thread of the original intact.

As per the latest buzz, Presenter Kamal Mukut maintained that the makers have complete faith in the movie and want audiences to see it as originally intended. He shared, “Our intention has always been to bring SURYAA: Ant Se Aarambh Tak to audiences exactly as it was envisioned. We strongly believe in the movie, its story and what it ultimately stands for. It is unfortunate that an entire narrative is being constructed around a few seconds of promotional footage when the complete movie has not been viewed.”

In further updates, He also stressed that the team respects the certification process but does not want its creative vision to be compromised. “We respect the certification process and are committed to following every required procedure. At the same time, we remain equally committed to protecting the creative integrity of the movie. We sincerely request the media fraternity and audiences to view the movie objectively and experience the complete story before arriving at any conclusions.”

On top of that, The makers have also clarified that Suryaa is not an attempt to portray the medical profession in a negative light. They shared the movie focuses on corruption, exploitation and organised malpractice by certain individuals, rather than making a sweeping statement about the entire medical fraternity. The team added that it has no intention of discrediting doctors who continue to serve patients with honesty and dedication.

The postponement comes amid objections from members of the medical fraternity. Earlier this month, the Delhi High Court refused to entertain a PIL seeking a stay on the Sunny Deol-starrer, which was scheduled to rollout on November 20. A bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma observed that a similar petition was already pending before a single-judge bench. It shared there was no need for another case on the same issue and asked the petitioners to join the ongoing proceedings instead. They were also allowed to continue raising their concerns with the relevant authorities.

title: Akshay Kumar faces a terrifying new enemy in Samuk motion poster; creature thriller to release on May 28, 2027
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Akshay Kumar is gearing up to explore a new genre with Samuk , and the movie's first look has already sparked curiosity. After Bhooth Bangla, Welcome to the Jungle and Haiwaan in 2026, the star has revealed his next big-screen outing. The makers have unveiled a motion poster, offering a glimpse into the movie's dark world and the terrifying threat at its centre. Set around a mysterious invasion, Samuk promises a blend of high-octane action, science fiction and survival horror. The movie is set for worldwide rollout in theatres on May 28, 2027.

Adding to this, Akshay Kumar dropped the first look motion poster of Samuk. Akshay Kumar unveils motion poster Akshay shared the motion poster on social media, giving followers a glimpse of the danger that awaits in the movie. Accompanying the reveal was a caption that read, “The enemy isn't human. But the fight is for humanity. And backing down isn't an option. SAMUK - The invasion begins 28th May, 2027.”

Meanwhile, The poster sets the scene in a dense, mist-covered forest, with Akshay dressed in a dark suit and holding a gun as he prepares to face an unknown threat. The biggest surprise comes when the creature finally appears. With its massive jaw, sharp teeth and dark fluid dripping from its mouth, the terrifying figure hints at the kind of enemy Akshay will be fighting.

Notably, Produced by Vipul Amrutlal Shah under the Sunshine Pictures banner, the movie is co-produced by Aashin A. Shah and directed by Kanishk Varma. The project brings together science fiction, action and horror, with a creature-led story that is an unusual choice for mainstream Indian cinema.

As per the latest buzz, Samuk also reunites Akshay and producer Vipula after 13 years. The two have previously collaborated on films such as Aankhen, Waqt: The Race Against Time, Namastey London, and Singh Is Kinng. Speaking about their reunion, Vipul shared in a note, After a gap of 13 years, starting a new journey with Akshay Kumar today is a very, very joyful, happy and proud moment for all of us. The ambition to create something better and bigger every single time with Akshay Sir has been the hallmark of our journey."

In further updates, The makers have brought on board an international team to handle the movie's creature effects and action. Alec Gillis, the Academy Award-nominated designer who has worked on the Alien and Predator films, will be responsible for bringing the creature to life. The action sequences, meanwhile, will be designed by British stunt coordinator Luke Tumber, whose previous credits include Mission: Impossible and the Venom films.
On top of that, Joining Akshay in the movie are Rukmini Maitra, Vineet Kumar Singh, Rajat Kapoor, Banita Sandhu and Swanand Kirkire. Samuk is set to rollout worldwide in theatres on May 28, 2027.

title: Ravie Dubey surprised as Thai fans go gaga over his Lakshman in Ramayana, reacts to being called an ‘international heartthrob’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Ravie Dubey is still getting used to the attention coming his way from audiences in Thailand. The star, who plays Lakshman in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana : Part 1, of late discovered that followers in the country have been sharing video edits of him on social media and even given him an affectionate new name. Calling him ‘P’Ravie’, Thai followers have been celebrating his performance, something the star admits he did not see coming.

Adding to this, Ramayana star Ravie Dubey is the new Thai fan favourite; star reacts to widely shared edits and his new nickname. Ravie Dubey reacts to his widely shared moment In conversation with India Today, Ravie recalled how he first came across the posts and edits. He shared, “It took me a little while to realise what was happening! A couple of days ago, I went on X and Instagram and started seeing these reactions and video edits with captions in Thai. That’s when it really hit me that people in Thailand were watching the movie and connecting with the characters. It made me smile. I’m deeply grateful that he’s being received with such warmth. And seeing that same affection come in for all the characters from places like Indonesia and Hong Kong as well, it’s really moving to see how far Ramayana is reaching.”

Meanwhile, The star was also asked about being called an international heartthrob, a tag that clearly caught him off guard. He added, “International heartthrob? I really don’t know what to say to that! From the day I was cast to now, when the movie is out and people are giving it so much love, my instinct has been to offer gratitude. I think gratitude and surrender are my preparation, if I can call it that.”

Notably, Ravie's newfound popularity has been particularly visible on X (formerly Twitter), where Thai followers have been sharing edits of his portrayal of Lakshman. Some of these videos feature music by BLACKPINK's Lisa, with followers expressing their admiration through captions and posts in Thai. The name ‘P’Ravie’ has also caught attention. In Thai culture, ‘P’ or ‘Phi’ is a respectful prefix used when addressing someone older or senior.

As per the latest buzz, Starring Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana, Ramayana: Part 1 was rolled out in theatres on November 5. The movie has found a strong audience in several international markets, particularly in Southeast Asia, where the Ramayana has deep cultural and religious significance. Apart from Thailand, viewers in Indonesia and Hong Kong have also been expressing their appreciation for the movie and its characters.

In further updates, The international response has also contributed to the movie's impressive ticket-window performance. According to trade reports, Ramayana: Part 1 has collected approximately ₹ 1,384.50 crore rupees worldwide in its first 11 days. Its India gross stands at ₹ 909 crore rupees, while overseas markets have contributed around ₹ 475.50 crore rupees, accounting for more than 34% of its worldwide earnings. Ramayana: Part 1 will be releasing in 2028.

title: Siang project strategic necessity due to China's mega dam plan: Arunachal CM amid protests
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Itanagar, Arunachal Pradesh Chief Minister Pema Khandu on Monday described the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project as a strategic necessity for India's water security and defence, citing concerns over China's reported plan to build a massive hydropower project on the Yarlung Tsangpo river in Tibet.

Adding to this, Siang project strategic necessity due to China's mega dam plan: Arunachal CM amid protests Interacting with journalists during a programme marking National Press Day, Khandu shared power generation was not the primary objective of SUMP, which was conceived mainly to regulate and monitor upstream water flows and protect downstream regions from possible adverse consequences of China's proposed dam.
Meanwhile, The Yarlung Tsangpo flows through Arunachal Pradesh as the Siang, before entering Assam as the Brahmaputra and Bangladesh as the Jamuna.

Notably, "China's reported plan to construct a 60,000-mw hydropower project on the river has raised concerns over the possibility of water storage or diversion and its potential impact on downstream areas," Khandu shared.
As per the latest buzz, China has incorporated the mega project into its five-year plan and as per reports laid its foundation stone in 2025, he shared.

In further updates, Despite India and Bangladesh seeking information, Beijing had not shared sufficient details about the project, while the absence of a binding international framework for water-sharing between the countries remained a concern, he added.
On top of that, Khandu shared the proposed SUMP would have a storage capacity of around 9.2 billion cubic metres , compared with the reported 5.2 BCM capacity of the Chinese project.
"This would enable India to regulate river flows and respond to possible changes in discharge," he shared.

title: Ram Gopal Varma claims Ramayana Part 1's budget is under ₹800 crore as he slams critics ‘jealous’ of its success, says sequel will earn 10 times more
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana has faced criticism over its portrayal of Sita as a warrior, with some also questioning the movie's casting. However, despite the backlash, the movie has crossed ₹ 1,300 crore rupees worldwide in just 11 days and continues to enjoy a strong run at the ticket-window. Amid its success, filmmaker Ram Gopal Varma , who has watched the movie twice, has claimed that the budget for Part 1 is less than ₹ 800 crore rupees and hit out at those he believed were jealous of the movie's success.

Adding to this, Ram Gopal Varma hits back at critics who are jealous of Ramayana's success. Ram Gopal Varma claims Ramayana Part 1's budget is less than ₹ 800 crore rupees On Sunday, Ram Gopal Varma took to X and penned a note about the euphoria surrounding Ramayana. He wrote, "Even for the best of my films she din’t do this, but my mother has been buying tickets of @malhotra_namit ‘s #Ramayana for the servants, watch men etc in the building complex she lives, and inspite of this kind of euphoria leading it to breaking all ticket-window records and fast emerging as the BIGGEST HIT EVER in INDIAN CINEMATIC HISTORY, still a lot of noise is being made by many jealous that the collections are still not enough because it’s 2000 cr a piece making it 4000 for 2."

Meanwhile, He then claimed that the budget for Ramayana: Part 1 was not even ₹ 1,000 crore rupees. He wrote, "I got to know that the actual cost of Part 1 is a little less than 800, and that includes mutually beneficial deals, global tax benefits, subsidy elements, etc which will all eventually bring the cost to less than that. And not only me, but any reasonably experienced, movie-maker by seeing the movie, can see the cost can’t be more than that. Also, many are stupid to assume that both parts will cost same. That’s like thinking the cost before the interval and post-interval will be the same in a movie ..I know of films where 50% of the cost was just the climax."

Notably, Ram Gopal Varma further claimed that a significant portion of the budget went towards creating the elaborate world of Ramayana, which could later be used as an asset for gaming and other ventures, as well as for the movie's second part. He lauded producer Namit Malhotra's long-term vision, adding that most Bollywood filmmakers, trade analysts and self-proclaimed experts might not fully understand this approach.

As per the latest buzz, He further shared that, given Ramayana's current box-office performance, Namit Malhotra could recover the entire cost of the first part, or possibly even both parts, through the first instalment itself. He added that the non-theatrical revenue from the first part and the earnings from the second could provide further financial gains. According to RGV, this could allow Namit to invest in several ambitious ventures that even the biggest production houses across North and South India have not been able to undertake, potentially putting him ahead of some of Hollywood's biggest names.

In further updates, Calling Namit the "biggest mega filmmaker", RGV added, "And the fact that the most fantastic action set pieces will be in part 2 starting from the Hanuman acts, Vaanar Sena, Ram Sethu, Lanka dhahanam, Sita in Lanka, Kumbha Karan’s death, Ravan vadh and many many more just to name a few, and going by the extraordinary proven Vision of Namit Malhotra’s combination of strategy, business acumen, creative understanding and visionary outlook, If KGF 2 did around 5 times more than KGF 1, I am convinced that Ramayana 2 will do 10 times more than Ramayana part 1...If you disagree, we will talk in 2028."

On top of that, The mythological epic stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Ravi Dubey as Lakshman and Yash as Ravana. Arun Govil, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Lara Dutta, Indira Krishnan and Sheeba Chaddha also feature in key roles. While the second part was initially scheduled to rollout in 2027, the makers have verified that the sequel has been pushed to 2028.

title: Sonu Sood meets Josh actor Sharad Kapoor after his emotional plea for work, checks on his health
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Josh star Sharad Kapoor of late made headlines after a video of him parting ways with his four pet dogs due to his health issues went widely shared. He later made an emotional appeal to his Bollywood colleagues, asking them to offer him work. A day after his plea, star Sonu Sood was spotted meeting Sharad and in conversation with him, as paparazzi captured their interaction.

Adding to this, Sonu Sood meets Josh star Sharad Kapoor in Mumbai. Sonu Sood meets Sharad Kapoor In videos shared by paparazzi on social media, Sonu is seen sitting with Sharad and talking to him, seemingly enquiring about his health. Sharad was also seen discussing his leg treatment with Sonu. After their conversation, the two actors shared a warm hug before Sonu escorted Sharad back to his building. Sharad was seen using a walking frame for support.
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Buzzzooka Prime (@buzzzookaprime)

Notably, According to a report by Free Press Journal, Sonu had arranged medical supplies for Sharad. The star is as per reports taking a keen interest in understanding Sharad's current situation and has been personally following up on his condition.

As per the latest buzz, Sharad moved his pets, Josh, Rebel, Star and Panther, to an animal welfare centre as he was unable to care for them due to his health issues. A video of him parting ways with his dogs subsequently went widely shared. His friend Hema Choudhary, who runs the Mumbai-based Bezubaan Public Welfare Trust, later shared an update on the star's health. She opened up that he had been struggling with physical and mental health issues for nearly two years, including a brain-related condition and a broken leg.

In further updates, The star later made an emotional appeal to his colleagues in Bollywood, asking them to offer him work rather than just financial assistance. In a video shared on Instagram, Sharad shared he was going through a difficult phase in his life and opened up that he had been battling depression. He expressed his admiration for senior actors and shared he hoped they would extend a helping hand during this time.
On top of that, “I really need help financially, morally, and mentally. I'm a big fan of all my senior actors. I always look at them as heroes," he shared.

He added, "I want to appeal to CINTAA that I am looking for good work. And I need your support, and I know you have always supported people around you. A little bit of moral support is also enough for me. I am a great star and you know that. Money is not the issue. The only issue is I am just looking forward to start work again".

title: Tanhaji: The Unsung Warrior and Adipurush director Om Raut to conduct masterclass on making grand films at Chitrapataka 2026
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

As per the official website of Chitrapataka, Om Raut will speak about the art of mounting films on a grand scale. The session will take place on Wednesday, November 11, at Ravindra Natya Mandir, an iconic performing arts theatre and cultural hub located in central Mumbai, near Siddhivinayak Temple.

Adding to this, The other prominent celebrities who will speak at Chitrapataka 2026 are director Laxman Utekar of Chhaava (2025) and Eetha (2026) fame, veteran actors Sachin Pilgaonkar and Dr Mohan Agashe, senior star Shubha Khote, director Tejas Prabha Vijay Deoskar of Bucket List (2018) and Ground Zero (2025) fame, etc.
Meanwhile, After completing his education, Om Raut worked as a writer & director for MTV Network in New York City. After returning to India, he became the creative head of DAR Motion Pictures.

Notably, He made his directorial debut with the Marathi flick, Lokmanya: Ek Yug Purush (2015), based on the life of Bal Gangadhar Tilak. It was a decent ticket-window success and received critical acclaim. Om Raut then made his debut in Bollywood with Tanhaji: The Unsung Warrior (2020), starring Ajay Devgn, Kajol and Saif Ali Khan. Based on the valour of Tanaji Malusare, the period action drama was a huge smash hit at the ticket-window. Tanhaji was followed by Adipurush (2023), based on the epic Ramayan. It starred Prabhas, Saif Ali Khan, Kriti Sanon and others. The movie was mounted on a huge scale but received widespread criticism for its screenplay, dialogues and visuals.

As per the latest buzz, Two years later, Om Raut rolled out his production, Inspector Zende (2025), starring Manoj Bajpayee and Jim Sarbh. It was rolled out directly on Netflix and was directed by Chinmay Mandlekar. In 2025, his soon-to-release directorial, Kalam: The Missile Man Of India , was revealed at the Cannes Movie Festival. It will feature Dhanush as Dr APJ Abdul Kalam.

title: Sonakshi Sinha files complaint over morphed photos, Delhi man released by Mumbai court
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

As per the latest buzz, Aryan was arrested at around 10:11 AM from the Jagatpuri Police Station area in Delhi's Shahdara. He was subsequently brought to Mumbai by flight and produced before a magistrate by the Bandra Police. The police had sought three days of custody, stating that they needed to recover the electronic device allegedly used to create and circulate the morphed photographs.

Adding to this, However, the court declined the police's request and questioned the procedure followed during the arrest. The magistrate raised concerns over why the accused had been brought directly from Delhi to Mumbai without first being produced before the nearest magistrate in Delhi, as required under the legal procedure.

Meanwhile, According to an India Today report, the magistrate observed that the police had failed to follow the prescribed legal process and had not provided a satisfactory explanation for bypassing the necessary procedure. The court's observations eventually led to Aryan's rollout.

Notably, During the hearing, his lawyers, Aman Shahi, Prashant Trivedi and Aditya Jain, also challenged the legality of the arrest. The defence argued that the police had neither served Aryan with the mandatory notice nor informed him about the reasons for his detention. They further questioned the urgency with which the arrest had been carried out.

As per the latest buzz, The lawyers also argued that the complainant's influential position may have influenced the police action. Maintaining that Aryan had not committed any offence, the defence contended that the legal provisions invoked against him were not applicable in the present case.

In further updates, The court's decision came after examining the procedural shortcomings highlighted during the hearing. While the police had sought additional custody to investigate the alleged circulation of the morphed photographs and trace the electronic device involved, the request was rejected due to the lapses in the arrest procedure.
On top of that, The matter comes after Sonakshi approached the authorities over the alleged circulation of objectionable manipulated images of herself on social media.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Sunny Deol’s Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak postponed to 2027; veteran actor still has 4 releases in 2026 after 19 YEARS
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

A source told Bollywood Hungama , “The IMA’s complaint has reached the Health Ministry. The makers are clear that they have no intention of showing the entire medical fraternity in a bad light or encouraging violence against medical personnel. However, there’s a due process to be followed in such situations, and since it is taking time, the makers have decided to postpone the rollout. They will first get the necessary clearances from the relevant authorities, secure the censor certificate from the Central Board of Movie Certification (CBFC) and only then announce the new rollout date.”

Adding to this, The source continued, “ Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak will now not be rolled out in 2026, as December is packed with back-to-back big releases in Hindi as well as English. Hence, the makers have decided to bring the movie to cinemas in 2027. One of the dates they are eyeing is January 15. However, a final call will be taken only after the issue is resolved.”

Meanwhile, According to a report in The Times of India, dated October 23, “IMA wrote to I&B ministry to urgently review the promotional content of Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak , alleging that it generalizes corruption in the medical profession and depicts violence against healthcare workers in ways that could erode public trust and put doctors’ safety at risk…In a letter, dated October 22, to I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, IMA national president Dr Anilkumar J Nayak sought an impartial review of the promo video for the soon-to-release movie and appropriate corrective measures from its makers. It also called for a ban or other action if justified under applicable law. The letter was also copied to the Union health and home ministries and the chairperson of the National Medical Commission”.

Notably, Interestingly, despite the postponement of Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak , Sunny Deol has had as many as four releases in 2026. While Border 2, Batwara 1947 and Ramayana arrived in cinemas, Ikka premiered directly on Netflix.

As per the latest buzz, In Ramayana , audiences got only a brief glimpse of Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman during the end credits. Nevertheless, it can be counted among his 2026 releases, especially since the star participated in the promotions and his casting added considerably to the movie’s hype.

In further updates, It is after a long time that Sunny Deol has had so many releases in a single year. Interestingly, the last time this happened was way back in 2007, when he also had four releases – Big Brother, Fool N Final, Apne and Kaafila .

title: Ramayana worldwide box office collection day 11: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, Sai Pallavi film grosses ₹1385 crore; beats Dhurandhar, RRR lifetime hauls
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Nitesh Tiwari’s Ranbir Kapoor , Sai Pallavi, Yash and Ravi Dubey-starrer Ramayana: Part 1 might have received mixed reviews worldwide, but it has had no bearing on its ticket-window performance. The movie had grossed over ₹ 1380 crore rupees worldwide after a weekend push, beating the lifetime collection of Aditya Dhar’s Ranveer Singh -starrer Dhurandhar. The movie has already beaten the collections of films such as Kalki 2898 AD, Jawan, KGF: Chapter 2 and more.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor plays Rama in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana adaptation. Ramayana worldwide ticket-window collections On day 11 of its rollout, its second Sunday, Ramayana collected ₹ 75 crore rupees net and ₹ 89.50 crore rupees gross at the domestic ticket-window. According to the trade website Sacnilk, this takes its domestic total to ₹ 760.60 crore rupees net and ₹ 909 crore rupees gross. Adding to that the ₹ 475.50 crore rupees the movie collected from overseas so far, with ₹ 40 crore rupees coming in just on Sunday, Ramayana’s worldwide collection stands at ₹ 1384.50 crore rupees gross. With Ramayana, India now has 11 films that have grossed more than ₹ 1000 crore rupees.

Meanwhile, This means that Ramayana now has Dangal ( ₹ 2000 crore rupees), Pushpa 2: The Rule ( ₹ 1871 crore rupees), Dhurandhar : The Revenge ( ₹ 1813 crore rupees), and Baahubali 2: The Conclusion ( ₹ 1788 crore rupees) to contend with. The movie has now beaten the lifetime collection of Dhurandhar, which stands at ₹ 1307.35 crore rupees. RRR grossed ₹ 1230 crore rupees worldwide, and KGF 2 grossed ₹ 1215 crore rupees. Pathaan and Jawan grossed ₹ 1055 crore rupees and ₹ 1160 crore rupees, respectively. Kalki 2898 AD brought in ₹ 1042.25 crore rupees.
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by The World Of Ramayana (@worldoframayana)

As per the latest buzz, Ramayana: Part 1, rolled out in a few regions as Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, is directed by Nitesh Tiwari, who co-wrote the screenplay with Shridhar Raghavan. It is produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash . The movie, which sees Ranbir play Rama, Sai as Sita, Yash as Ravana, and Ravi as Lakshmana, is based on multiple iterations of the epic, including the Valmiki Ramayana.

In further updates, The first part charts Ram and Ravana’s journey from childhood to adulthood, the 14-year exile, and Sita’s abduction. It is narrated by Anupam Kher, who voices Jatayu in the movie. Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Kunal Kapoor, Adinath Kothare, Arun Govil, Indira Krishnan, and Lara Dutta play key roles in it.
On top of that, Ramayana ends by setting up the story for Ramayana: Part 2, which will be rolled out for Diwali 2028. Sunny Deol will play Hanuman in the sequel.
