title: Twinkle Khanna calls Ravana the 'original tech bro', compares him to tech billionaires Jensen Huang, Bill Gates
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

You can always trust Twinkle Khanna to have an unfiltered take on everything making news. Of late, the star-turned-writer shared her thoughts on Ranbir Kapoor and Yash's movie Ramayana . In her latest column, Twinkle compared Ravana to a few tech billionaires, including Jensen Huang, Elon Musk and Bill Gates, calling him the 'original tech bro'.

Adding to this, Twinkle Khanna took a swipe at tech billionaires in her latest column. Twinkle Khanna compares Ravana to tech billionaires In her column for The Times of India, Twinkle recalled Ranbir Kapoor's past remark about Elon Musk's Tesla Roadster and Ravana's Pushpak Viman. Ranbir, who plays Lord Ram in Ramayana, had shared, “India invented a flying car 5,000 years ago.”

Meanwhile, Taking a cue from Ranbir's observation, Twinkle described Ravana as 'the blueprint for the original tech bro'. She drew parallels between the mythological king and some of the world's most powerful businessmen, referring to the controversies surrounding their personal lives and alleged affairs.

Notably, She mentioned Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his alleged affair with Alice Huang, how he had to step down from the company he had built for over three decades after the affair came to light. She also mentioned Bill Gates and the scrutiny he faced following revelations about his alleged affairs. Twinkle noted that Ravana had the intelligence and ability to conquer the world but failed to master his own mind, much like some powerful men today.

As per the latest buzz, Drawing comparisons between Ravana and the billionaires, she wrote, "Ravana was exceptionally learned, wealthy, powerful and had access to remarkable tech. He also believed that he was above the rules that governed others. Add the obsession with immortality, and the similarities between him and today's tech billionaires are hard to ignore."

In further updates, She further added, “All Ravana needs is a leather jacket, a device on each of his ten heads, a Silicon Valley HQ with his own podcast, and he would blend right in. Ravana had the intelligence and ability to master the world, but like so many powerful men, failed to master his own mind.”

On top of that, Ramayana is a two-part cinematic adaptation of the Hindu epic, directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra. The movie features music by Oscar-winning composer Hans Zimmer and AR Rahman.
The first part was rolled out on November 5, with the second part expected to follow in 2028.

title: ‘Highest priority’: Centre responds to Neha Bora ahead of Delhi-NCR toxic air protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Union environment ministry responded late on Sunday evening to an email from All India Students’ Association (AISA) president Neha Bora, asserting that minister Bhupender Yadav attaches the “highest priority” to tackling air pollution in Delhi-NCR and is continuously monitoring enforcement measures across states.

Adding to this, Bora revealed the plan to visit the minister’s office on Monday. (Sanjeev Verma / Hindustan Times) In an email to Bora, who has asked people to head to Yadav’s Jor Bagh office on Monday afternoon, the ministry also noted that the minister is currently in Türkiye leading the Indian delegation at the COP31 climate summit.

Meanwhile, Bora revealed the plan to visit the minister’s office on Monday, saying her initial request for an appointment to discuss air pollution and its impact on citizens’ health had gone unanswered. Asked whether she would proceed with the plan after the ministry’s response, AISA shared its programme “remains unchanged”.

Notably, On Monday morning, the Jawaharlal Nehru University Students’ Union (JNUSU) also revealed it would join the citizens’ delegation marching to the minister’s office to fight for their “Right to Breathe”.

As per the latest buzz, Delhi’s air quality index (AQI) remained in the ‘poor’ category on Monday morning. The city recorded an AQI of 218 at 8am, falling in the ‘poor’ category. After touching 207 at 3am, the 24-hour rolling AQI average has started reversing its downward trend and is expected to deteriorate further during the day.

In further updates, In a video rolled out on Sunday, Bora sharply attacked the government over the air crisis in Delhi-NCR, saying she requested an urgent meeting with the minister on November 12 over worsening air pollution and the public health crisis, but received no response. “Either you have people like Bhupender Yadav, who, amidst a public health emergency, are quiet – or you have people like Rekha Gupta or Mohan Bhagwat, who are giving all sorts of unscientific excuses to justify pollution...” she shared in her video, urging people to reach outside the minister’s office for the right to breathe and the right to life.
On top of that, In its response late on Sunday, the ministry shared Yadav was “continuously monitoring and reviewing” the measures taken by state governments and local authorities.

“In his last meeting with the Delhi NCR states held on November 11, the NCR states have been directed to ensure strict, time-bound and coordinated ground-level enforcement including deputation of secretary-level senior officers in each city of Delhi NCR states to closely monitor the enforcement actions,” the email shared. HT has reviewed the response sent by V Pazhaniyandi, director in the ministry.

title: Soni Razdan had ‘no clue’ she was pregnant with Alia Bhatt while shooting Gumrah, recalls smoking 100 cigarettes in a day
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Alia Bhatt continued working through her pregnancy and even shot for her Hollywood debut, Heart of Stone, while expecting her daughter. She seems to have inherited that work ethic from her mother, star Soni Razdan , who also continued working during both her pregnancies. In a recent interview with Screen, Soni recalled shooting while pregnant with Alia and opened up that she had smoked around 100 cigarettes in a day while filming a scene.

Adding to this, Soni Razdan recalls shooting Gumrah while being pregnant with Alia Bhatt. Soni Razdan recalls smoking 100 cigarettes while pregnant with Alia Bhatt Soni recalled getting pregnant for the first time while shooting for the 1986 television show Buniyaad. She spoke about how the Sippy family, who produced the show, went out of their way to make things comfortable for her. At the time, she was living in Lokhandwala, which was not a developed area, and finding a taxi early in the morning was difficult. Since she and her husband had only of late started their married life and did not own a car, the production team arranged one for her so she would not have to worry about transport at 6 am. She added that she was given the best room on the set and was well looked after throughout the shoot.

Meanwhile, She then recalled getting pregnant with Alia while shooting for the 1993 crime thriller Gumrah. Soni shared, "I was shooting that smoking scene, and I’d have smoked some 100 cigarettes in one day. I had no clue Alia was inside me! I’m not a smoker, but after that, I was just craving cigarettes. I also did that famous gallows scene when I was pregnant with her. Then there was a big break. Five months later, when I came back, my costumes wouldn’t fit me. I had a little bump by then. So, we had to alter the costumes."

Notably, Soni Razdan and filmmaker Mahesh Bhatt got married on April 20, 1986. Their relationship began after they met during the making of Mahesh's 1984 movie Saaransh, in which Soni played a prominent role. The couple welcomed their first daughter, Shaheen Bhatt, in 1988, followed by Alia Bhatt in 1993.

title: Tamannaah Bhatia joins Chhath Puja celebrations in Mumbai, shares video after The Vvaan's festive sequence won hearts
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Tamannaah Bhatia of late joined devotees at Chhath Puja celebrations in Mumbai. The star posted on Instagram to share a video from the celebrations, in which she was seen interacting with followers and taking part in the festivities. Tamannaah of late featured in The Vvaan: Force of the Forrest, and the movie's Chhath Puja sequence received much love from audiences. Its portrayal of the festival struck a chord with several viewers.

Adding to this, Tamannaah Bhatia celebrates Chhath Puja. Tamannaah Bhatia celebrates Chhath Puja Sharing videos from the Mumbai celebrations, Tamannaah thanked devotees for their affection and sought the blessings of Chhathi Maiya. “Devi ka aashirwad, aur aap sabka pyaar, Chhathi Maiya ki kripa bani rahe! Chhathi Maiya ki Jai! (The blessings of the goddess and the love of all of you — may Chhathi Maiya's grace remain with us. Hail Chhathi Maiya),” she wrote.
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Tamannaah Bhatia (@tamannaahspeaks)

Notably, The Vvaan received mixed reviews, but its Chhath Puja song struck a chord with audiences. Composed and arranged by Vishal Mishra, with lyrics by Kaushal Kishore, the song reminded many viewers of their own celebrations and connection with the festival.
As per the latest buzz, During the promotions of The Vvaan, Tamannaah spoke about how she made an effort to understand Chhath Puja before filming the song sequence.

In further updates, “I have always held a deep reverence for Chhath Puja. Before we started shooting for the song, I spent time studying and understanding the significance of the ritual and how it is performed in Bihar and Patna. Honestly, I was stunned to learn about the power it holds. The strong connection I felt with Chhathi Maiyya is something I cannot put into words. I found myself feeling deeply connected to her. Chhath Puja is one of the most important aspects of The Vvaan, and I would not have wanted to experience the ritual in any other way,” she shared.

On top of that, Of late, Sidharth Malhotra spoke about how The Vvaan was written off before its ticket-window success. During his appearance on Koffee With Karan, he shared, “I think they are doing their job and we are doing our job. There is an India, and there is a Bharat. I think Bharat is what is coming out to watch our films. They want to watch something rooted, something for them and rooted in culture. The Vvaan came perfectly fitting that bracket, whether it is the writing, performance, or sequences.”

Starring Sidharth Malhotra, Tamannaah Bhatia, Shweta Tiwari, Sunil Grover and Anup Soni, The Vvaan: Force of the Forrest was rolled out in theatres on September 25. Directed by Deepak Kumar Mishra, the movie draws inspiration from folklore surrounding the Van Devi temple in Bihta, Bihar. It also explores the spiritual and cultural significance of Chhath Puja.

title: Supriya Pathak reveals Pankaj Kapur threatened to walk out if their wedding lasted over an hour, kept checking time
body: Here's the latest relationship update doing the rounds:

Sooraj Barjatya, along with the cast of Yeh Prem Mol Liya , of late appeared on The Great Indian Kapil Show . During the episode, Kapil Sharma showed the guests pictures from their weddings, prompting them to reminisce about their special days and share anecdotes about their relationships with their partners.

Adding to this, Supriya Pathak reveals Pankaj Tripathi's unusual deadline on wedding day. Supriya Pathak recalls Pankaj Kapur's one-hour deadline for wedding During a segment on the show, Kapil displayed wedding pictures of Sooraj Barjatya, Ayushmann Khurrana, Seema Pahwa, Supriya Pathak and others. When a picture from Supriya and Pankaj Kapur's wedding appeared on screen, Kapil pointed out that Pankaj looked rather "angry".

Meanwhile, Supriya then revealed the reason behind his serious expression. She shared in Hindi, "Pankaj Kapur and I have been married for 38 years. At our wedding, Pankaj had given a deadline. He shared if the wedding didn't happen in one hour, he would walk out. He kept checking the time every few minutes to see if it was done or not."

Notably, Ayushmann also spoke about his relationship with his wife, Tahira Kashyap, and shared, "I have been married for 17 years. I was close to the same age as Soorajji when he got married; I was 24. Tahira and I were in the same tuition, physics first, then chemistry, and later biology. I was 17 when we started dating. During my wedding, I had refused to ride a horse or wear a sehra, but Sooraji made me do all of it in this movie."

As per the latest buzz, Veteran actors Supriya Pathak and Pankaj Kapur got married in 1988 after falling in love while working together on the unreleased movie Agla Mausam. Both had been married previously and had separated from their respective partners before beginning their relationship. The couple dated for around two years before tying the knot. body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Ramayana is unstoppable at the ticket-window. The Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash-starrer rolled out in theatres on November 5 amid high expectations. Followers showered it with positive reviews and the extended Diwali holiday weekend proved beneficial for the movie as it saw a huge growth on Monday and Tuesday. Post Diwali, the movie remained steady and now on its second weekend, the movie has scored Bollywood's biggest second Sunday.

Adding to this, Star Ranbir Kapoor is portraying Ram in the movie Ramayana Ramayana ticket-window update Advance bookings for Ramayana opened on Dussehra, 15 days before rollout. By the time of its rollout, the movie had already sold tickets worth ₹ 200 crore rupees worldwide. The movie went on to collect ₹ 64.85 crore rupees in India on its first day of rollout, becoming the fourth-highest opening in Bollywood history. The movie then collected ₹ 107 crore rupees net on Monday and ₹ 94 crore rupees net on Tuesday, both the highest in Indian cinema history.

Meanwhile, As per the latest update on Sacnilk, Ramayana managed to collect ₹ 75 crore rupees on its second Sunday, showing further growth than Saturday's ₹ 72.90 crore rupees haul. This brings the total ticket-window earnings of the movie to ₹ 760.60 crore rupees .

Notably, Ramayana has now delivered the biggest second Sunday for a Bollywood movie at the ticket-window, beating Ranveer Singh's Dhurandhar 2. The spy thriller, which rolled out in theatres earlier this year in March, had collected ₹ 68 crore rupees. The highest second Sunday haul is still held by ₹ 76.60 crore rupees.

As per the latest buzz, Meanwhile, the movie has already surpassed the lifetime haul of Shah Rukh Khan's Jawan ( ₹ 643.87 crore rupees) and Rajkummar Rao's Stree 2 ( ₹ 625.27 crore rupees). It also overtook Chhaava (which stood at ₹ 601.57 crore rupees). Previously, it had crossed lifetime hauls of Shah Rukh Khan's Pathaan (which stood at ₹ 544.28 crore rupees) and Ranbir Kapoor's previous theatrical rollout Animal (which stood at ₹ 556.36 crore rupees).

In further updates, Ramayana is the latest adaptation of Valmiki's epic, one of the world's oldest pieces of literature. It tells the story of Lord Rama, the incarnation of Lord Vishnu and his battle against the asura king Ravana after the latter abducts his wife, Sita.

On top of that, Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman. title: Ravie Dubey humbled by all the love for his portrayal of Lakshman in Ramayana, recalls feeling scared that he would disappoint everyone
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Ravie Dubey is basking in the praise for his performance as Lakshman in Ramayana Part 1. The movie, which stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama and Sai Pallavi as Sita, rolled out in theatres on November 5. It has crossed ₹ 1,000 crore rupees in worldwide collections within eight days of its rollout. On Sunday, Ravie shared a heartfelt note on his Instagram to thank viewers for all the love for his portrayal of Lakshman in the movie.

Adding to this, Ravie Dubey shared BTS stills from the shoot of Ramayana. Ravie's statement Taking to his Instagram, Ravie shared a carousel of pictures from the shoot of Ramayana. In one picture, he was seen standing on the set in costume. In another picture, he was seen holding the bow and arrow for a scene. The star was also seen with co-stars Ranbir and Sai in one picture. In the caption, Ravie began, “On the morning of 5th November 2026, I woke up and felt something I’d forgotten the feeling of. I felt ‘seen’, and the love in it felt infinite.I think that’s all an star truly wants. That someone gives your work a chance. That something you felt while doing it reaches someone else, and they feel enough to tell you about it. What a gift that is. I’m still in disbelief as I write this. All I feel is gratitude.”
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ravie Dubey (@ravidubey2312)

Notably, He added that he felt connected with the character of Lakshman, sharing, “Shri Lakshman had no ambitions for himself he was content to stand a step behind Shri Ram and Maa Sita, ready for duty whenever they needed him. I found that so beautiful, so noble. In whatever small measure I could, I wanted to bring that same feeling of service and duty to Ramayana and be ready when I’m called upon. Offer All i could mentally ,physically and spiritually . That was truly all I wanted but You all rewarded me with so much more.”

As per the latest buzz, Ravie thanked casting director Mukesh Chhabra and director Nitesh Tiwari for choosing him for the part and treating him with so much love. “@castingchhabra bhai, that one call from you has truly changed my life m so grateful, @iamnamitmalhotra sir, @niteshtiwari22 sir, you are rare human beings & iam indebted you put me on a set with the greatest talent in the world. A set where I was the most junior and the least accomplished, and yet from the day I walked in, you gave me just as much love, just as much respect and just as much room to do my work.”

In further updates, The star recalled that he was scared to take up the part. "What if I’d disappointed these incredible people who trusted me with some thing so important ? What if I’d done too little? What if I’d gone overboard? What if i’d done a disservice to Shri Lakshman, to Ramayana itself. And then came your love. I wish I could tell each of you what it has done for me. There’s so much joy in it, of course. But there’s also a very tender relief. To have served Ram Katha in even the smallest way fills my heart . I’m sure my ancestors, wherever they are, are leaping with joy." he added.

On top of that, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. title: Josh actor Sharad Kapoor seeks work after battling depression and health issues, says he needs help ‘financially, morally, and mentally’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Sharad Kapoor is hoping to return to acting after being away from work for the past few years due to health issues and depression. The star, best known for playing Prakash Sharma in Shah Rukh Khan's Josh , has now appealed to the movie industry to consider him for projects, making it clear that he is looking for work and not financial assistance.

Adding to this, Sharad Kapoor seeks work after health setbacks and depression; AICWA urges movie industry to support him. The star of late found himself in the news after a video of him parting ways with his four pet dogs went widely shared. Unable to care for them because of his health, he had moved his pets Josh, Rebel, Star and Panther to an animal welfare centre. Now, the star is looking forward to getting back on his feet and returning to the sets.

Meanwhile, In a video shared on Instagram on Sunday, Sharad reached out to senior members of the movie fraternity, saying he was going through a difficult phase and could use their support. His appeal came a day after the news about his four dogs being moved to an animal welfare centre caught the attention of social media users.

Notably, “When somebody blames you for nothing, you obviously feel pained by it. I went into depression. I didn't feel like working or meeting anybody,” Sharad shared in the video. He was as per reports referring to the sexual harassment case registered against him by Mumbai Police in 2024, after a 32-year-old star and producer accused him of groping her. “But now, I've decided. I appeal to the movie industry; please help me. Whatever financial crisis I have, I want to work and get out of it," he added.

As per the latest buzz, The star also opened up that he has been bedridden for the past two to three years. Speaking about the support he has received from his family, Sharad shared that they mostly check on him through occasional phone calls. He also expressed his admiration for senior actors and shared he was hoping they would extend a helping hand during this phase. “I really need help financially, morally, and mentally. I'm a big fan of all my senior actors. I always look at them as heroes," he shared.

In further updates, Meanwhile, his friend Hema Choudhary, who runs Mumbai-based Bezubaan Public Welfare Trust, shared an update on the star's health. She opened up that he has been struggling with physical and mental health issues for nearly two years, including a brain-related condition and a broken leg. Star Jaya Bhattacharya, who visited the star after his video went widely shared, also shared a clip in which he spoke about his situation.

On top of that, View this post on Instagram Addressing the speculation surrounding his finances, Sharad clarified that he was not seeking monetary help. Instead, he wants an opportunity to return to acting and some support from the movie fraternity. "I want to appeal to CINTAA that I am looking for good work. And I need your support, and I know you have always supported people around you. A little bit of moral support is also enough for me," he shared in the video. "I am a great star and you know that. Money is not the issue. The only issue is I am just looking forward to start work again".

Last seen in the 2019 movie Cabaret, Sharad opened up that he has spent much of the past two to three years bedridden. He also opened up about the emotional toll of a sexual harassment case registered against him in 2024, which he has previously denied. The star shared the allegations took a toll on his mental health, pushing him into depression and making him distance himself from work and social interactions.

title: Vinod Kapri says he was warned of ‘serious repercussions’ for speaking up as Pyre faced screen cuts amid Ramayana release
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

National Award-winning filmmaker Vinod Kapri has opened up that several people in the movie industry warned him against speaking out about the reduction in screenings of his independent movie Pyre amid the rollout of Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash in the lead roles. The filmmaker shared he was cautioned about facing 'serious repercussions' and the possible impact his stand could have on his future in the industry. However, Vinod chose not to back down, maintaining that he had every right to question what happened to his movie and stand up for smaller towns that often struggle to get independent cinema into theatres.

Adding to this, Vinod Kapri says he was warned against taking on the industry over Pyre’s reduced shows amid Ramayana rollout. Vinod Kapri on warnings from industry insiders In conversation with SCREEN about the advice he received after raising the issue publicly, he shared several people had asked him to be careful and warned him that speaking against the system could have consequences. However, the filmmaker believes staying silent was not an option.

Meanwhile, Explaining why he decided to take a stand, he shared, “Many people told me not to speak up because I have to continue working in this industry and there could be serious repercussions. I told them I don’t want to be part of this industry in that way. I made this movie while staying outside the industry. I don’t want to cast big actors, nor do I think they would work with me. I want to continue telling these simple stories. If I don’t stand up for my rights and for my towns today, who will?”

Notably, He added, “Theatre owners also have their hands tied. They are under a lot of pressure. This is the first time I have seen something like this in cinema, where you are not allowing another movie to be screened, even if your theatres are going to remain empty. You would rather have empty theatres than screen another movie. It was really upsetting."

As per the latest buzz, Announcing the movie's return to more screens after getting limited screens during Ramayana rollout, Vinod took to social media and of late wrote, “PYRE IS GETTING ITS SHOWS BACK! Over 200 shows of PYRE are being added from Friday, 13th November. A heartfelt thank you to our audiences for standing by this little independent movie and making this possible. Your love, trust and support have brought us back to more screens.”

In further updates, He also thanked Cinepolis and PVR Cinemas for supporting the movie and helping it reach a wider audience. The announcement came after days of uncertainty over its theatrical run, with Vinod repeatedly speaking about the difficulties faced by smaller films when competing with major releases.

On top of that, Made on a reported budget of ₹ 2.5 crore rupees, Pyre initially opened with around 80 shows. Positive word of mouth helped the movie gain momentum, and its screenings as per reports increased to over 400 within a few days. However, Vinod claimed that the movie lost nearly 75 percent of its shows after Ramayana arrived in theatres on November 5.

The row also prompted the All India Cine Workers Association (AICWA) to write to Union Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw. The association has sought a fair screen allocation policy, an impartial inquiry into the reduction of Pyre's shows and action against those found responsible. AICWA also stressed the importance of giving independent films a fair opportunity in theatres, noting that smaller productions play a key role in shaping the future of Indian cinema.

body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Ranbir Kapoor 's Ramayana has had a terrific run at the ticket-window, crossing the ₹ 1000 crore rupees mark worldwide within just nine days of its rollout. The Nitesh Tiwari-directed movie, which hit theatres on November 5 during the Diwali festive season, has continued to draw audiences in India and overseas. Titled Ramayana: Rise of a Legend in international markets, the mythological drama features Ranbir as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. The movie is the first part of a two-movie saga, with the second instalment expected to rollout in 2028.

Adding to this, Ramayana's ticket-window rampage continues! Movie crosses ₹1,200 crore rupees worldwide, Dhurandhar 2 stays on top. Ramayana ticket-window earnings According to the trade tracker Sacnilk, Ramayana saw another strong day at the ticket-window on Saturday. On day 10, the movie collected ₹ 72.90 crore rupees net in India across 23,451 shows. The movie's total India gross has now reached ₹ 819.50 crore rupees. After adding ₹ 30 crore rupees, the movie's overseas gross stands at ₹ 408.50 crore rupees. This takes its worldwide collection to ₹ 1228 crore rupees in just ten days.

Meanwhile, While Ramayana has recorded an impressive day 10 collection in India, it is still trailing Aditya Dhar and Ranveer Singh's Dhurandhar: The Revenge at the worldwide ticket-window. The movie continues to hold the top spot, despite Ramayana's rapid growth over the past few days. By day 10, Dhurandhar 2 had recorded ₹ 1255.41 crore rupees collection at the ticket-window.

Notably, However, Ramayana's journey to the ₹ 1000 crore rupees club has been faster than several major Indian blockbusters. Only Pushpa 2: The Rule and Dhurandhar: The Revenge reached the milestone sooner, taking seven days each. Ramayana managed it in nine days, beating Baahubali 2, which took 10 days, RRR, which needed 16 days, and KGF: Chapter 2, which took 18 days. It has also reached the milestone much faster than Shah Rukh Khan's Jawan and Pathaan. While Jawan took 18 days to cross ₹ 1000 crore rupees worldwide, Pathaan took 27 days. Ramayana's numbers reflect the strong response the movie has received across its different language versions and international markets.

As per the latest buzz, The movie's ticket-window success is not its only recent achievement. Ramayana will also be the first movie screened in the BRICS segment at the 57th edition of the International Movie Festival of India (IFFI), which is scheduled to begin in Goa on November 20. According to the Press Information Bureau (PIB), the segment will feature films from all 11 BRICS member countries, as well as partner nations. The initiative aims to bring films from around the world to Indian audiences and showcase a range of cinematic styles and stories.

Kunal Kapoor , who played Indra in the movie, found himself gaining a whole new fanbase, with audiences from other countries penning poems and creating artwork. The star acknowledged the love and shared that he was overwhelmed by it.

Adding to this, Kunal Kapoor plays Indra in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana adaptation. Kunal Kapoor overwhelmed by love from Southeast Asia On Sunday, Kunal shared posters of him as Indra from Ramayana on X (formerly Twitter), writing, “Indra. Phra In. Batara Indra. Thagyamin. Preah En. Taishakuten. One king of the heavens, known by different names across many lands. It’s incredible how much we have in common.”

Meanwhile, He further wrote, “I’ve been overwhelmed by the love pouring in for Lord Indra from India, from Thailand and across Southeast Asia, and from so many corners of the world I never expected to hear from. Thank you, truly. I’ve always believed good stories have a way of connecting us all, and our cultures share more of them than we realise. It means the world to see a timeless epic like the Ramayana find so much love, everywhere.”

Notably, Kunal ended his note with, “And to all the wonderful artists who have created such beautiful art, and continue to do so, thank you so much. I’m sorry I don’t know each of your handles, but I’ve seen your work and it means a lot.”

As per the latest buzz, In Ramayana: Part 1, Kunal plays a cameo as Devraj Indra, the king of devas. He appears in two pivotal battle scenes, one of which sees him facing off against Ravana. He also appears in a scene in which he urges Vishnu to take a new avatar to fight Ravana, who has grown powerful after receiving a boon from Brahma.

In further updates, The star has now been receiving love from Thailand for his role, with followers sharing his clips and pictures from Ramayana with comments such as, “Found him! The golden-skinned one. His beauty is like Indra, descended from heaven to Earth, radiant as the moon, above the land of heaven, above all other men. The Indra of Thai people's dreams,” and “As radiant as Indra, descended from heaven to earth, as beautiful as the moon. May I humbly invite your majesty to Thailand.”

On top of that, After Kunal acknowledged the love he has been receiving, a fan even wrote, “Lord Indra is already aware of it! The love sent by Thai followers has truly reached him—how lovely! It’s wonderful that #Ramayana has served as a bridge, strengthening the bond between Thailand and India. Thai people have likely wanted to express their affection for a long time; after all, they have always watched and been captivated by Indian films, and there is a very devoted fan base here.”

Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. The first movie hit screens on November 5 and has grossed ₹ 1228 crore rupees worldwide in 10 days. The second part will be rolled out in theatres for Diwali 2028.

title: Sonakshi Sinha files complaint over morphed photos, man arrested in Delhi later released by Mumbai court
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Sonakshi Sinha had approached the police after allegedly finding objectionable morphed photographs of herself being circulated on social media. Following her complaint, the Bandra Police registered a case and arrested Delhi-based Aryan Deepak Jain in connection with the matter. However, a Mumbai court has now ordered his rollout, rejecting the police's request for three days' custody due to lapses in procedure during his arrest.

Adding to this, Sonakshi Sinha case: Man arrested over morphed nude photos rolled out as court flags BNSS violations. Aryan was arrested around 10:11 AM from the Jagatpuri Police Station area in Delhi's Shahdara and brought to Mumbai by flight. The Bandra Police subsequently produced him before a magistrate, seeking his custody to trace the electronic device allegedly used to create and circulate the morphed photographs. The court, however, questioned the police for bringing him directly from Delhi without first producing him before the nearest magistrate there.

Meanwhile, According to an India Today report, the magistrate questioned why Aryan Deepak Jain had been brought straight from Delhi to Mumbai without first being presented before the nearest magistrate in Delhi. The court noted that the police had not followed the required legal process and had failed to offer a satisfactory reason for the lapse.

Notably, His lawyers, Aman Shahi, Prashant Trivedi and Aditya Jain, also questioned the legality of his arrest. They told the court that the police had neither served him with the mandatory notice nor informed him of the reasons for his detention. The defence also raised questions over the haste with which the arrest was carried out, arguing that the complainant's influential position may have influenced the police action. They maintained that Aryan had not committed any offence and that the legal provisions invoked against him were not applicable.

As per the latest buzz, The magistrate also questioned whether the police had followed the arrest guidelines laid down under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). Since the alleged offences carry a maximum jail term of seven years, the investigating officer was required to record why his arrest was necessary, as mandated under Section 35(1)(b) of the BNSS.

In further updates, The court further pointed out that the need to investigate the matter was not, by itself, sufficient to justify taking Aryan into custody without following the prescribed legal procedure. "The mere requirement of further investigation cannot, by itself, justify arrest and detention without following the statutory safeguards," the court observed.

On top of that, The magistrate turned down the police's request for three days' custody and ordered Aryan's rollout due to procedural lapses in his arrest. However, the case is far from over, with the Bandra Police continuing their investigation into Sonakshi's complaint.

Monica Yadav is a senior entertainment journalist with Hindustan Times Entertainment, based in Mumbai, with nearly 11 years of experience covering Bollywood, Hollywood and Asian entertainment, including Korean, Chinese and Thai cinema, television and music. She is among the few Indian journalists in India with a dedicated focus on Korean entertainment, including K-pop and K-dramas, and has interviewed some of the industry's biggest stars while closely tracking the rise of global pop culture. Alongside her work at Hindustan Times, her bylines have appeared in several international publications. title: HT Leadership Summit 2026: Imtiaz Ali and Ananya Panday talk love, changing dynamics of cinema
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

What does it feel like to be a filmmaker in India today? “It’s a delicious phase,” shared acclaimed director Imtiaz Ali , speaking at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit on Saturday. In an interaction with Sonal Kalra, HT’s chief managing editor for entertainment and lifestyle, Ali and star Ananya Panday discussed love stories, shifting trends, and the power of sometimes breaking the rules.

Adding to this, Imtiaz Ali and Ananya Panday discussed love and cinema at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit on Saturday. ((HT Photo)) Panday, 28, spoke about nepotism, safety on sets, her dream roles, and how “love is everything”. “I think Gen-Z is badnaam [notorious] for no reason,” she shared, smiling.

Meanwhile, There is the sense that young people do not want to fight hard for success, she added, but “it’s just our definition of success that’s different. Earlier, the sentiment was that if you hadn’t slogged mentally and physically, you hadn’t worked hard enough.” But success can now be achieved in so many different ways. “The way we approach success is different.”
Notably, Attention spans are changing, Ali noted. “We are all asking: What will work?”

As per the latest buzz, On the other hand, he added, distributors are seeing how varied the audience has become in its tastes. “The same people that watch [the movie] Ramayana will also want to watch [the independent movie] Pyre . Distributors know this.”

In further updates, This makes the calculation of what will work, and how, more complicated, shared Ali, 55. In June, he rolled out his 10th directorial feature, the Partition-themed love story Main Vaapas Aaunga , to widespread acclaim. Did he worry, before the rollout, that young viewers might not relate? He didn’t, he shared.
On top of that, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Hindustan Times (@hindustantimes)

India loves stories with big emotions, Ali noted. Rather than attempting to woo a specific demographic, Ali added, “We should ask ourselves: What is a story I can tell; and try to tell it.” Stop looking for patterns; this has become a unique obsession of our times, he shared. “Sometimes randomness works… the movie industry is trying to break the pattern.” Discussing his recent rollout further, Ali talked about the importance of exploring the horrors of Partition, particularly from the perspective of a third-generation person now navigating this history. It isn’t just that people of all ages respond to a powerful tale, Ali noted. Young people in particular engage with stories of “big love and big loss” because they see it in films and read about it in books, but do not have as much of it in their young lives. “They can relate to it in a way previous generations would not.”

title: Katrina Kaif calls Vicky Kaushal the ‘peace to her hysteria’ as she talks about juggling business, marriage, motherhood

Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Vicky Kaushal (@vickykaushal09)

title: Addinath Kothare met Ranbir Kapoor in school, recalls auditioning for Lakshman before landing Bharat's role in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana | Interview
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Addinath Kothare has steadily made his mark across Marathi and Hindi cinema. In 2019, his directorial Paani, in which he also played the lead role, won the National Movie Award for Best Movie on Environment Conservation. He has since continued to explore different projects, including Kabir Khan's 83, several web series and the of late rolled out Nayyi Naveli. The star is now seen as Bharat in Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana , also known internationally as Ramayana: Rise of a Legend. In a conversation with Hindustan Times, Addinath talks about initially auditioning for Lakshman before being cast as Bharat, working with Ranbir Kapoor, filming the emotional Bharat Milap sequence and why he considers the filmmaker's screenplay a masterclass.

Adding to this, Addinath Kothare calls Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana screenplay a masterclass, recalls getting emotional during narration. (Sunil Khandare) Landing the role of Bharat was not an overnight process. The star went through several rounds of auditions over several months before being finalised for the part. He also opens up about working with Nitesh Tiwari and Ranbir, and the experience of shooting one of the movie's most emotional moments, the Bharat Milap sequence.

Meanwhile, Addinath and Ranbir have an interesting connection that goes back to their school days. Both actors studied at Mumbai's Bombay Scottish School, and the star still has a faint memory of seeing Ranbir on the school premises when he was in the seventh standard.

Notably, He shares how a common friend, Binoy Gandhi, who lived in his building and is now a filmmaker, introduced him to Ranbir. “I remember seeing Ranbir in school. I had a common friend who used to stay in my building. He is also a filmmaker today; his name is Binoy Gandhi. He had introduced me to Ranbir once in school. I have a very vague memory of this tall, thin person sitting on the railing of the senior building. I was probably in the seventh standard,” he recalls. Addinath also reveals that he may have brought up the school memory during a later conversation with Ranbir. Interestingly, he believes the star also remembered the incident.

As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram From auditioning for Lakshman to playing Bharat Addinath reveals that his association with Ramayana began with an audition for the role of Lakshman, which eventually went to Ravie Dubey. The casting process, led by Mukesh Chhabra, required him to perform a scene in which Lakshman asks Sita to stay inside the kuti (forest hut) before drawing the rekha (line), requesting her to not step out for safety reasons. Looking back, the star believes the audition was also about finding actors who could convincingly look like a family on screen. “I tested for the scene where Lakshman tells Sita to stay in the kuti. That was probably a benchmark test to find the family of Shri Rama because we all had to look like we belonged to the same family,” he recalls.

In further updates, It was nearly six months after the audition that Addinath received a call informing him that he had been shortlisted. The experience also reinforced his belief that auditions are not just for newcomers and that established actors should be equally open to the process. He feels there is a misconception that actors with experience should not have to audition. “There is a completely wrong notion that people have about auditions. Nobody comes to theatres just to see faces. They come if they like the story. Today, there is so much talent around us. Even if there are 10 good actors, it does not necessarily mean all of them will get the right opportunities,” he says.

On top of that, Talking about why he continues to audition despite having years of experience, Addinath points out that casting is about finding the star who fits a particular character best. He adds, “There are so many actors who can play a particular part. How will the director decide who is right for it? Today's casting directors are experimenting and giving opportunities to new and fresh faces. As actors, we need to help filmmakers push their boundaries. Auditions are very crucial. Internationally, even A-list actors audition.”

The star also credits Mukesh Chhabra for giving him opportunities to audition for several projects. He believes the process has value even when an audition does not lead to a role, as it allows actors to showcase their abilities and gives casting directors a chance to consider them for future projects.

title: Ramayana box office collection day 10: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer crosses ₹670 crore, beats Stree 2, Jawan lifetime hauls
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana , starring Ranbir Kapoor , Yash and Sai Pallavi, rolled out in theatres on November 5. The movie did great business on its opening day, setting a new record for a pre-Diwali rollout in India. However, the collections hit a dip on the second day, given it was a non-holiday and right before the weekend. It picked up with great speed on Monday and Tuesday, over the extended Diwali holiday period.

Adding to this, Ramayana stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama and Yash as Ravana. Ramayana ticket-window update Advance bookings for Ramayana Part 1 opened on Dussehra, 15 days before rollout. By the time of its rollout, the movie had already sold tickets worth ₹ 200 crore rupees worldwide. The movie went on to collect ₹ 64.85 crore rupees in India on its first day of rollout, becoming the fourth-highest opening in Bollywood history. Ramayana entered the elite 500-crore rupees club on Wednesday.

Meanwhile, As per the latest update from Sacnilk, Ramayana collected ₹ 61.25 crore rupees. It is a huge jump from the last few days' haul, taking full advantage of the second weekend at the ticket-window. This brings the total collection to ₹ 673.95 crore rupees so far. Ramayana has now surpassed the lifetime hauls of Shah Rukh Khan's Jawan (which stood at ₹ 643.87 crore rupees) and Rajkummar Rao's Stree 2 (which stood at ₹ 625.27 crore rupees). Earlier, the movie had crossed the lifetime haul of Shah Rukh Khan's Pathaan and Ranbir Kapoor's previous rollout, Animal.

Notably, Ramayana is the latest adaptation of Valmiki's epic, one of the world's oldest pieces of literature. It tells the story of Lord Rama, the incarnation of Lord Vishnu and his battle against the asura king Ravana after the latter abducts his wife, Sita.

As per the latest buzz, Produced by Namit Malhotra ’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part movie. The movie stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman. The first rolled out worldwide on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2028.

In further updates, Ramayana Part 1 will be the opening movie of the BRICS segment at the 57th edition of the International Movie Festival of India, which will showcase films from all 11 member countries, along with contributions from partner countries, offering audiences an opportunity to explore diverse cinematic traditions and storytelling from across the BRICS nations, as per the press rollout shared by Press Infomation Bureau of India.

title: HT Leadership Summit 2026: Ananya Panday calls herself a greedy actor, shows interest in mythology while praising Ramayana
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Ananya Panday and filmmaker Imtiaz Ali were guests at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit on Saturday. The duo spoke about cinema to HT's Sonal Kalra, and the star opened up about everything from women's representation in cinema to the kind of roles she would love to play. She also expressed an interest in mythology while praising Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana.

Adding to this, At the HT Leadership Summit, Ananya was asked if she watched Ramayana and shared, “I did. Blown away, love, love loved it.” She recalled growing up hearing Indian mythological tales from her mother and grandmother, leading to her interest in mythology.

Meanwhile, Expressing interest in starring in a mythological movie in the future, she added, “I think it’s just a fabric of our society as Indians to tell stories and have them passed down from generation to generation. Palace of Illusions is one of my favourite books, so that’s all I’m going to say.” Chitra Banerjee’s 2008 novel The Palace of Illusions is a retelling of the Mahabharata told from Draupadi’s perspective.

Notably, Ananya also spoke about the kind of roles she would like to play in the future. “I like everything; I am a very greedy star. I want to be able to do every possible thing,” she shared. The star also added that she loved crying on screen, chalking it up to her not being an emotional person in real life. “I find a lot of actors saying that. They really love going there emotionally. I do enjoy comedy a lot; I feel like it’s very freeing,” she added.

As per the latest buzz, Ananya also spoke about Indian cinema having space for everything from testosterone-pumping films to female-led ones. “We also have films like Lokah or Gangubai or Kahaani or Piku. Imtiaz sir is such an example of how he has created a balance between male and female emotions. There would be no Rockstar without Heer. It’s not that she exists in relation to him. He also exists in relation to her. I think he has created that so beautifully. So, we always have examples of films where women are shining, and I don’t think it’s just about a movie where the woman is the central character,” shared the star.

In further updates, Ananya last starred in the romantic drama Chand Mera Dil with Lakshya as her co-star. The movie was directed by Vivek Soni and produced by Dharma Productions. It starred her alongside Lakshya.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Writer-director Imtiaz Ali was one the speakers on the 24th edition of the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit 2026, where he spoke at length about the changing landscape of the Hindi movie industry. The filmmaker, whose last rollout Main Vaapas Aaunga went on to become a surprise hit at the ticket-window, picked the example of Dhurandhar and lauded the movie's daring to break many rules.

Adding to this, Imtiaz Ali spoke about Dhurandhar at the Hindustan Times Leader Summit. What Imtiaz shared During his conversation with Sonal Kalra, Chief Managing Editor, Entertainment and Lifestyle, Hindustan Times at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit, Imtiaz shared, “I feel something very interesting is happening in the movie industry. We are in that delicious phase where people are saying that nothing is working. Should we go with the big star, non-star… what is going to work? People are saying that attention span is missing in the audience but the films which are doing well are three hours long. nothing long is working. People are citing Dhurandhar as an example of what is successful but look at the length of that movie!”

Meanwhile, He added, “Forgetting the fact that when Dhurandhar was actually conceived and it was doing its run around those studios, people thought that this is the most impractical, a movie with the least likelihood of success! But it broke all the rules and after that everybody wants to make that. All of us are thinking what will work. The language might change but I feel its a phase of introspection that the movie industry is going through.”

Notably, Aditya Dhar's two Dhurandhar films have grossed over ₹ 3000 crore rupees at the ticket-window. Rolled out in December, the first Dhurandhar movie, starring Ranveer Singh , was a critical and commercial success. It collected a then-record ₹ 841 crore rupees net in India, and courtesy of a $33 million overseas haul, crossed ₹ 1300 crore rupees gross worldwide. After a rather long run in theatres that lasted over 14 weeks, Dhurandhar ended its run at ₹ 1308 crore rupees.

As per the latest buzz, The sequel, Dhurandhar: The Revenge, arrived in March and shattered every Bollywood box-office record. The movie became the first from Hindi cinema to net ₹ 100 crore rupees in a single day, a feat it achieved three times during its opening weekend. It sailed past ₹ 1000 crore rupees in a week and soon surpassed its predecessor. As of April 16, Dhurandhar 2 has collected just over ₹ 1025 crore rupees net in India and ₹ 1720 crore rupees worldwide. The makers claim the worldwide gross exceeds ₹ 1760 crore rupees. Either way, the Dhurandhar franchise has crossed ₹ 3000 crore rupees worldwide, with the upper estimate at ₹ 3110 crore rupees for the two films.

In further updates, Written and directed by Aditya Dhar, Dhurandhar is a spy thriller starring Ranveer Singh as an Indian spy infiltrating the gangs and terror networks of Pakistan. The films also star R Madhavan, Akshaye Khanna, Arjun Rampal, Sanjay Dutt, Rakesh Bedi, and Sara Arjun. The first part was critically acclaimed, while the second received more lukewarm reviews. However, both are the two highest-grossing Hindi films in India.

title: HT Leadership Summit 2026: Imtiaz Ali never thought Main Vaapas Aaunga was a risky film, says ‘there was no Pakistan, only undivided India’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmaker Imtiaz Ali and star Ananya Panday were guests at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit on Saturday. While there, the duo spoke about cinema and discussed their work to HT's Sonal Kalra. Imtiaz spoke about his recent rollout, Main Vaapas Aaunga , which appeals to Gen Z despite being set during the India-Pakistan partition. He also remarked that the movie was not depicting Pakistan, just an undivided India.

Adding to this, Imtiaz argued that his movie wasn’t risky because it didn’t depict Pakistan. “I knew that there was no Pakistan in my movie; it was undivided India,” he pointed out, adding, “Because those portions lay across a border that was later established.”

Meanwhile, Imtiaz shared that meeting many who lived during the Partition inspired the tale: “I felt that meeting a lot of individuals that have seen Partition from their own eyes, and listening to their stories, I realised that the narration of the third generation of partition survivors is missing in the media space now. We don’t know how a 75-year-old person views partition now, 78 years after the Partition and independence of the country. His view is very different from the first-generation refugee.”

Notably, Talking about the movie’s subject further, Imtiaz shared that those who lived through Parition tend to remember beautiful moments more than the immediate anger or loss they felt then. "This is the victory of human emotion, I feel. That it tends to remember the beautiful things, happy things, rather than the negative ones. I learnt this in meeting these elderly gentlemen and ladies that have gone through partition. And this was not represented in cinema. So I thought, I must do this. And I must do this at the time when some of them are still with us.”

As per the latest buzz, Imtiaz reiterated that he never believed Main Vaapas Aaunga had anything that would potentially hurt anyone, stating, “No, I wasn’t ever thinking that there’s going to be anything in the movie that is going to be controversial or hurtful to anybody. I never thought it’s a risky movie.”

In further updates, Imtiaz also spoke about how he always believed that Main Vaapas Aaunga would appeal to Gen Z, stating, “Nobody told me that Gen Z will not relate, because I’m very convinced that the Gen Z more than anyone will relate to a painful love story. I think painful love story is their thing. That’s because some of them miss it. Some of them miss the kind of commitment that they see in films or read in books in their own life. It has become difficult to get into that kind of situation or commitment.”
On top of that, Main Vaapas Aaunga was rolled out in June and stars Naseeruddin Shah, Diljit Dosanjh, Sharvari, and Vedang Raina in lead roles. It is available to stream on Netflix.

title: Soha Ali Khan digs out childhood pictures of parents Sharmila Tagore, Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi with Nehru on Children's Day
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Every year on November 14, Children’s Day is celebrated to mark the birth anniversary of India’s first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru. On the day, star Soha Ali Khan took to her Instagram to post childhood pictures of her mom, star Sharmila Tagore, and dad, cricketer Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi, aka Tiger Pataudi, with Nehru. She remarked on the significance of the occasion in her caption.

Adding to this, Sharmila Tagore and Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi with Nehru. When young Sharmila Tagore, Tiger Pataudi met Nehru Soha posted three monochrome pictures on her Instagram account. One picture shows a young Sharmila pinning something onto Nehru’s coat. Another picture shows her standing beside him at the All India Radio (AIR). The third picture she posted shows Tiger sitting next to Nehru during an unknown occasion.
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Soha (@sakpataudi)

Notably, “Before they were my parents, they were children too. Today, on Children’s Day, which marks the birth anniversary of Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, I’m sharing two special glimpses from our family albums,” wrote Soha in her caption, adding, “My mother as a little girl, my father as a boy, alongside a man who believed that children were the future of the nation.”

As per the latest buzz, Soha further wrote about how Nehru’s birthday turned into Children’s Day, adding, “Pandit Nehru ji's birthday became Children’s Day in India because he didn't want the day to be about himself - he wanted to celebrate the future of the nation, our children and to give each of them an opportunity to dream big.”

In further updates, She ended her note with a wish for all the children of the country, writing, “My parents had big dreams - with talent, hard work. perseverance and opportunity their dreams came true. May every child have the same chance turn their dreams into reality. Happy Children’s Day!”

On top of that, Sharmila and Tiger met at an after-match party in 1965 and dated for about four years, during which he would woo her with everything from roses to air conditioners. They even lived together before their wedding in 1968. In June this year, Sharmila, while in conversation with Barkha Dutt, recalled that everyone was sceptical about their relationship. “ Yash Chopra told me, 'These Nawabs are very doubtful people, so you have to be very careful.' He was a good friend and genuinely concerned,” she shared.

On Siddharth Kannan’s show, Sharmila’s eldest daughter, Saba Ali Khan Pataudi, opened up that her mother had converted to Islam for the marriage, as was the norm at the time. Their three children, Saif Ali Khan, Saba and Soha, were born in 1970, 1976 and 1978 respectively. Tiger died at the age of 70 in 2011.

title: Bollywood’s new security blanket: More bouncers, 6-7 security personnel being provided for celebs during public appearances
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Reports of a security advisory asking Bollywood celebrities to avoid public appearances following the firing incident at star Tiger Shroff’s Mumbai residence sparked concern in the movie industry earlier this week. The reports also claimed that several celebrities’ homes had allegedly been surveyed by suspects. However, Mumbai Police denied issuing any such advisory. Manoj Kumar Sharma, Joint Commissioner of Police (Law & Order), Mumbai, clarified, “This is not true and does not reflect facts. Please verify information thoroughly before publishing any such news.”

Adding to this, Tiger Shroff While the incident has prompted heightened caution, star appearances and event commitments continue. Talent management company owner Rakesh Upadhyay, who works with actors including Ravi Kishan, Ameesha Patel and Jacqueline Fernandez, says, “While actors have definitely become more cautious, there has been no major change in the number of events celebrities are taking on. If they are performing at a company or event organised by a businessman, star managers now ask for the link to their website, how many people will attend and details about the guests. The demand for security has increased in number. From 3-4 bouncers we now arrange 6-7 for the celeb. Other than that there has been no major change.”

Meanwhile, A source associated with the Shroff family’s public appearances says Jackie Shroff has continued honouring his commitments. “Jackie sir has always been bindaas (fearless) and nothing much has changed there he has been keeping up his commitments, without any fuss. However, with many other clients the demand for security has increased, six bouncers is the minimum number being demanded now and all information about the organisers is verified thoroughly by our team.”

Notably, Trade analyst Girish Johar believes fewer promotional appearances are unlikely to hurt box-office collections: “The ticket-window numbers depend on strong content, lack of movie promotions in person will not majorly affect ticket sales. Shah Rukh and Salman Khan have already cut down their promotional appearances but it did not affect their ticket-window numbers at all.”

title: Neetu Kapoor recalls mother-in-law Krishna Raj Kapoor’s reaction after she and husband Rishi Kapoor missed her Diwali celebrations
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The Kapoor family like to spend festivals together, and were known for their grand celebrations during Diwali. Raj Kapoor also hosted lavish Diwali parties for the entire family. In a recent chat with Curly Tales, Neetu Kapoor shared an anecdote about her mother-in-law, Krishna Raj Kapoor, after she and husband Rishi Kapoor missed one such Diwali party due to prior work commitments.

Adding to this, Krishna Raj Kapoor with Neetu Kapoor and Ranbir Kapoor. What Neetu shared Neetu shared that the Kapoor family love to eat together and during the celebrations the entire table would be a spread of several delicacies. Neetu shared that Raj Kapoor loved to see the whole clan together as they shared the same table at RK Studios. During Diwali, everyone would gather at Raj Kapoor and Krishna Raj Kapoor’s home in Chembur after finishing the puja at their respective homes.

Meanwhile, Neetu shared, "Mom used to have these envelopes ready for everyone. One time we missed going to the Chembur home because we were late and Rishi had some work and was caught up in that. The next day when we went and she took out the envelope, took out the money, and she tore the envelope.”

Notably, “She shared, ‘You don’t deserve it. I missed you yesterday’. It’s just that she had so much love. She just commanded love, she didn’t demand it," recalled Neetu. In those envelopes, she would gift cash to her near and dear ones. Neetu shared that she has kept that tradition alive and now gifts envelopes to her family during Diwali.

As per the latest buzz, This Diwali, Neetu shared a picture with son Ranbir Kapoor and daughter-in-law Alia Bhatt on Instagram. A framed picture of late husband Rishi Kapoor was seen behind them in the picture.
In further updates, View this post on Instagram A post shared by neetu Kapoor. Fightingfyt (@neetu54)

On top of that, Krishna Raj Kapoor, wife of legendary star Raj Kapoor, died in 2018 due to a cardiac arrest. She was 87. Meanwhile, Rishi Kapoor died in 2020, at the age of 67 following a two-year battle with leukemia (specifically acute myeloid leukemia), a type of blood cancer.

Neetu was last seen in Daadi Ki Shaadi alongside her daughter Riddhima Kapoor Sahni. Her son, Ranbir Kapoor, is currently basking in the success of Ramayana Part 1 where he plays Lord Rama. The movie is directed by Nitesh Tiwari and rolled out in theatres on November 5.

title: ‘Youngsters don’t want false promises': Akhilesh Yadav on youth, CJP and recent protests
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Samajwadi Party has always stood with young people, shared party supremo Akhilesh Yadav on Saturday, when asked about his views on the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and the protests led by the outfit, one of which led to the resignation of education minister over examination irregularities.

Adding to this, SP supremo Akhilesh Yadav at HT Leadership Summit 2026 in New Delhi on Friday, November 14 “When these young people saw how the government was playing with their children's futures, they came out and protested. Not just the students, but their parents also joined them. This movement has made people more aware,” Akhilesh Yadav shared at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit 2026.
Meanwhile, Gen Z and the younger generation are clear about what they want, he shared, adding that they do not want false promises. “They want clarity about what is possible and what is not.”

Notably, “Given the reach of social media and the penetration of the internet in society today, you cannot get away with lying to people. Ultimately, even the Prime Minister had to acknowledge the issue, and a minister had to be removed. That was the biggest achievement of the youth,” Yadav shared.
As per the latest buzz, He shared he was happy to see youth from UP and Bihar turn up in large numbers to the protests.

In further updates, “I am happy that during the protests, young people from Uttar Pradesh and Bihar came to Delhi in large numbers and participated. They came on their own. Nobody helped them or made arrangements for their food, water, accommodation…,” Yadav shared.

title: Tinnu Anand discharged from hospital after 14 days, recovering at home following five fractured ribs and punctured lung
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Veteran star-filmmaker Tinnu Anand , who suffered five fractured ribs and a punctured lung after a fall, says he has been discharged from the hospital and recovering at home. He was discharged from Kokilaben Dhirubhai Ambani Hospital in suburban Mumbai on Thursday, where he was admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) following the accident.

Adding to this, Tinnu Anand recovering at home following five fractured ribs and punctured lung. Tinnu Anand is recovering at home In conversation with PTI, the star shared an update on his health and shared he was feeling much better. "I've come home after 14 days and I'm much better now. I'm supposed to recover in the bed, till the doctors says, 'You're okay to go out'," he shared.

Meanwhile, The 81-year-old director shared he had a fall at his residence. Recalling how the accident happened, Tinnu shared he fell while walking around his house at night when the lights were switched off. He did not immediately realise the extent of his injuries and only learnt about the fractures the following morning.

Notably, "I was walking in the night and the lights were not on, and suddenly I fell down and went to sleep after that. The next morning, I came to know that I've suffered a fracture so my daughter took me to the hospital. After the CT scan, we learnt that I've got five fractures. I don't remember how I spend that time but I'm okay now," he shared.

As per the latest buzz, The star has been advised complete bed rest as he continues his recovery. He is also undergoing physiotherapy at home and is taking time to regain his strength following the injuries. "I'm resting well at home," he shared, adding that he hopes to resume work on two South-language films sometime next month, depending on his recovery and his doctors' advice.

In further updates, Tinnu Anand has been a part of the Hindi movie industry for decades, wearing several hats as an star, filmmaker, writer and director. The son of veteran screenwriter Inder Raj Anand, he comes from a family with deep roots in cinema. While a younger generation of viewers may recognise him from films such as Salaar, Ghajini, Dabangg and Merry Christmas, the filmmaker is equally remembered for his work behind the camera. As an star, his filmography also includes Agneepath, Khiladi, Damini, Kohra, Krantiveer, Trimurti, China Gate, Saathiya and Bluffmaster. As a filmmaker, he has also directed several films starring Amitabh Bachchan , including Kaalia, Shahenshah, Main Azaad Hoon and Major Saab.

title: Finding roles I want remains a struggle, willing to wait for right opportunities: Aditi Rao Hydari
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Mumbai, Star Aditi Rao Hydari says finding the kind of work she aspires to do continues to be a struggle but she is willing to wait for the right opportunities.

Adding to this, Finding roles I want remains a struggle, willing to wait for right opportunities: Aditi Rao Hydari The star, best known for her work in Hindi and South language films like "Delhi 6", "Padmaavat", "Kaatru Veliyidai", "Sammohanam", "Hey Sinamika" and OTT shows such as "Jubilee" and "Heeramandi", shared her choice of roles is not guided by a deliberate attempt to experiment with different characters.

Meanwhile, "I do things because I want to do them. If my heart says do it, then I do it. Also, for me the choice is based on the director and the writing. And I really work hard and I always wanted to be in a place where amazing directors choose me, which doesn't come easy," Hydari told PTI in an interview.
Notably, "I believe that the right people will find me for the most beautiful parts. I want to explore things, I want to learn, I always want to be a curious kid," she shared.
As per the latest buzz, The star, who made her acting debut in 2006 with the Malayalam movie "Prajapathi" co-starring Mammootty, shared she has to keep proving herself with every project.

In further updates, "I'm not saying this with resentment, and I'm not complaining either. Since I'm not from the industry, I've to prove myself every time. And when I say prove, I mean that you really have to believe, and stick your ground and be like, 'I'll not say yes to something that I don't want to do'."
On top of that, Hydari shared she continues to approach her career with patience and self-belief that the right opportunities will come her way.

"I believe, whether it is a manifestation or hard work, but I want to be in that place and I think I am kind of there. But every step is one uphill step even now, it is as much a struggle to get the kind of work that I want to do. I have to wait for it but I will wait for it," she shared.

title: BREAKING: Most violent Godzilla film ever, Godzilla Minus Zero NOT rated ‘A’ in India despite R rating overseas; CBFC grants U/A 16+ certificate
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

We have now learned that the censor process of Godzilla Minus Zero is complete. As per the website of the Central Board of Movie Certification (CBFC), the Japanese monster flick has received a U/A 16+ rating on November 13.

Adding to this, Interestingly, Godzilla Minus Zero received an R rating and equivalent adult classifications across most major international markets, including the USA, UK, Australia, etc., marking a rare departure for a major theatrical Godzilla entry. The R rating generated significant excitement among core followers, horror enthusiasts, and cinephiles. Followers largely celebrated the rating as proof that the makers have gone all out with the depiction of violence. With Godzilla Minus Zero not receiving an 'A' certificate in India, it now remains to be seen if the CBFC has passed the movie without cuts or censored the disturbing shots.

Meanwhile, In fact, it has often happened that films that are allowed to be consumed for the under 18 population gets a harsher rating in India. A recent example was The Devil Wears Prada 2 . In most countries, it was allowed to be seen for audiences of all ages. However, in India, it was passed with an 'A' rating, shocking moviegoers. Many argued that it should have got a clean 'U' rating from the CBFC.

Notably, The length of Godzilla Minus Zero , as mentioned on the censor certificate, is 137.25 minutes. In other words, the movie is 2 hours, 17 minutes and 35 seconds long. It'll have a rollout in IMAX screens in India as well.

title: Telangana BJP chief put under ‘house arrest’ to prevent protest against Rahul Gandhi’s visit
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Telangana Police on Saturday placed Bharatiya Janata Party’s state unit president N Ramchander Rao under house arrest and detained hundreds of BJP workers across the state to prevent them from staging protests against Congress leader Rahul Gandhi’s visit to Hyderabad and the Congress-organised ‘Bharat Summit’ at HITEX in Madhapur.

Adding to this, Telangana BJP President N. Ramchander Rao placed under house arrest. (PTI) A statement from Rao’s office shared scores of police personnel gathered at his residence at Tarnaka and prevented him from coming out of his house to stop the conduct of Bharat Summit.

Meanwhile, Strongly condemning the police action, Rao alleged that the Congress government was adopting an authoritarian approach by preventing the BJP from exercising its democratic right to stage peaceful protests.
Notably, “Police personnel have been deployed in large numbers outside my residence from 6 am and prevented me from leaving the house,” Rao told reporters later.

As per the latest buzz, “You can’t stop the BJP with illegal house arrests," Rao wrote on X. "Rahul Gandhi has no moral right to set foot in Telangana! What’s happening in Hyderabad is an ‘Anti-India Summit’ that tarnishes the country’s prestige. The Congress has cheated the people by failing to implement its 6 guarantees, job calendar and Rythu Bandhu. The Progressive Alliance is conspiring with foreign powers to bring about a ‘regime change’ in the country,” he added.

In further updates, The BJP state president shared party workers, including members of the BJP Yuva Morcha, were also placed under house arrest or taken into preventive custody in several districts while they were preparing to stage demonstrations with black flags against Rahul Gandhi’s visit and the summit.

On top of that, Ramchander Rao maintained that the event was neither an investment summit nor a programme aimed at promoting Telangana's industrial development. Instead, he alleged, the Congress was using public money to organise a platform for foreign delegates to discuss India's internal political affairs and project a negative image of the country and the Narendra Modi government before the international community.

He questioned the rationale behind inviting foreign individuals who, according to him, had previously expressed anti-India views. Referring to Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng , who as per reports claimed on social media that her visa had been cancelled shortly before her scheduled visit, he questioned why individuals critical of India had been invited to the event.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Blockbuster filmmaker Ali Abbas Zafar debuts as composer, lyricist, singer with Parivarik ManuRanjan; turns his inside joke with Ranveer Singh and Arjun Kapoor into 'Sir Sir Sir' song
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

With Parivarik ManuRanjan , Ali Abbas Zafar has made his debut as a music composer. He has composed the song 'Jingle Bell' and is also one of its lyricists. For 'Sir Sir Sir' , Ali has gone a step further – he is the sole composer and lyricist, and has also lent his voice to the song alongside Vishal Mishra.

Adding to this, Bollywood Hungama exclusively spoke to Ali Abbas Zafar to understand what prompted him to take the musical plunge. Ali explained, “I have liked listening to music since childhood. Over a period of time, I have worked on films where music has been an important part of storytelling. So, I had some ideas in terms of tunes. And as they say, necessity is the mother of all inventions! The budget of this movie ( Parivarik ManuRanjan ) was very tight. Meanwhile, I had composed a few tunes by humming or playing them on the guitar. So, I suggested a few tunes for this movie. Our director, Varun V Sharma, reacted very positively to them. All those songs are now in the movie.” He added, “There are three songs that I have composed.”

Meanwhile, 'Jingle Bell' appears at a crucial juncture when Ranjan Dubey's (Pankaj Tripathi) life changes for the better following the entry of Manu (Aditi Rao Hydari). 'Sir Sir Sir' , meanwhile, is a foot-tapping number that plays during the birthday celebrations of Ranjan's boss.

Notably, Interestingly, during the promotions of Gunday (2014), Ranveer Singh, in his trademark entertaining style, had opened up that Ali Abbas Zafar had a habit of repeatedly saying “Sir Sir Sir”. When reminded of this amusing anecdote, Ali laughed and shared, “Yes. It was a code word between Ranveer, Arjun Kapoor and me.”

As per the latest buzz, He then explained the context behind 'Sir Sir Sir' , saying, “And yes, I used to say that. Go to any government office and you'll see this jargon used by employees while addressing their bosses. They don't simply say ‘sir’ when the boss instructs them or tells them something. They repeatedly say it. So, if the boss says, ‘Tomorrow, we'll have lunch together’, instead of saying, ‘Yes, sir’, the employee would say, ‘Sir, sir, sir’! If the boss instructs, ‘Shukla ki file leke aao’ , the reply would be ‘Sir, sir, sir’ instead of ‘Sir, I'll get the file’.”

In further updates, He added, “So, it's a part of the local context. When people in central India watch this movie, particularly the ‘Sir Sir Sir’ scene and song, they'll understand and enjoy it. This is how the whole system works.”
On top of that, Ali also had words of praise for the movie's director, Varun V Sharma. He shared, “Varun has always been very close to me as he was my assistant and co-writer on Bharat.”

Parivarik ManuRanjan 's director, Varun V Sharma, also spoke exclusively to Bollywood Hungama about Ali Abbas Zafar's musical contribution. He revealed, “During the editing process, we insert temporary music to establish a rhythm in the scenes. Similarly, I had put some music in an early scene, where ‘Jingle Bell’ was eventually used. Now, Ali sir has a great sense of music, which is why his films like Mere Brother Ki Dulhan, Gunday, Sultan , etc. were peppered with memorable songs. He also keeps composing tunes for his own interest and can even play the keyboard.”

title: Ramayana worldwide box office collection day 9: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, Sai Pallavi's epic sails past ₹1100 crore, beats Pathaan, Kalki 2898 AD

It added another ₹ 23 crore rupees from overseas markets on the ninth day, taking its worldwide collection to ₹ 1151.19 crore rupees.
